1.1.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red
1.1.1.definition: Testable Red is a group of 14 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir….

1.1.1.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Cabernet Sauvignon
1.1.1.1.definition: Red wine grape of Bordeaux origin, a natural cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc; thick-skinned and tannic, widely planted worldwide.

1.1.1.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Merlot
1.1.1.2.definition: Red wine grape from Bordeaux, softer and earlier-ripening than Cabernet Sauvignon; a major blending partner on Bordeaux's Right Bank.

1.1.1.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Pinot Noir
1.1.1.3.definition: Thin-skinned red grape of Burgundy, also a core Champagne grape; known for light-to-medium body and sensitivity to site.

1.1.1.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Syrah/Shiraz
1.1.1.4.definition: Red grape from the northern Rhône (Syrah), called Shiraz in Australia; deeply colored with peppery, dark-fruit character.

1.1.1.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Grenache/Garnacha
1.1.1.5.definition: Warm-climate red grape (Garnacha in Spain), central to Southern Rhône blends and Priorat.

1.1.1.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Tempranillo
1.1.1.6.definition: Spain's leading red grape, the backbone of Rioja and Ribera del Duero (where it is called Tinto Fino).

1.1.1.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Sangiovese
1.1.1.7.definition: Italy's most planted red grape and the base of Chianti, Brunello di Montalcino and Vino Nobile.

1.1.1.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Nebbiolo
1.1.1.8.definition: Late-ripening, high-tannin, high-acid red grape of Piedmont, used for Barolo and Barbaresco.

1.1.1.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Malbec
1.1.1.9.definition: Red grape originally from southwest France (Cahors), now best known from Argentina.

1.1.1.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Zinfandel/Primitivo
1.1.1.10.definition: Red grape genetically identical to Croatian Tribidrag; known as Zinfandel in California and Primitivo in Puglia.

1.1.1.11.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Cabernet Franc
1.1.1.11.definition: Red grape from Bordeaux and the Loire; a parent of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.

1.1.1.12.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Gamay
1.1.1.12.definition: Red grape of Beaujolais, making light, fruity reds.

1.1.1.13.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Barbera
1.1.1.13.definition: High-acid, low-tannin red grape of Piedmont, Italy (e.g. Barbera d'Asti, Barbera d'Alba).

1.1.1.14.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Mourvèdre/Monastrell
1.1.1.14.definition: Late-ripening red grape of Spain (Monastrell) and southern France (Mourvèdre, e.g. Bandol).

1.1.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White
1.1.2.definition: Testable White is a group of 12 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling….

1.1.2.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Chardonnay
1.1.2.1.definition: White grape of Burgundy and Champagne; flexible in style from lean and unoaked to rich and barrel-fermented.

1.1.2.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Sauvignon Blanc
1.1.2.2.definition: Aromatic white grape from the Loire and Bordeaux, typically high in acidity with herbaceous or citrus aromas.

1.1.2.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Riesling
1.1.2.3.definition: Aromatic white grape most associated with Germany and Alsace; high acidity, made from bone-dry to very sweet.

1.1.2.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Pinot Grigio/Gris
1.1.2.4.definition: Grey-pink-skinned mutation of Pinot Noir; called Pinot Grigio in Italy and Pinot Gris in France.

1.1.2.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Chenin Blanc
1.1.2.5.definition: High-acid white grape of the Loire Valley, made dry, sweet and sparkling; also important in South Africa.

1.1.2.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Gewürztraminer
1.1.2.6.definition: Very aromatic, pink-skinned white grape (an aromatic form of Savagnin), notable in Alsace.

1.1.2.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Viognier
1.1.2.7.definition: Aromatic white grape of the northern Rhône (Condrieu).

1.1.2.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Albariño
1.1.2.8.definition: Aromatic, high-acid white grape of Rías Baixas (Spain), called Alvarinho in Portugal.

1.1.2.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Grüner Veltliner
1.1.2.9.definition: Austria's signature white grape, often with peppery notes.

1.1.2.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Sémillon
1.1.2.10.definition: White grape of Bordeaux, the main grape of Sauternes and prone to noble rot.

1.1.2.11.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Torrontés
1.1.2.11.definition: Aromatic white grape and Argentina's signature white.

1.1.2.12.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Assyrtiko
1.1.2.12.definition: High-acid white grape originally from the Greek island of Santorini, making mineral, dry whites.

1.1.3.definition: Rosé is a group of 5 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Provence rosé, Tavel, Rosado (Navarra)….

1.1.3.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rosé › Provence rosé
1.1.3.1.definition: Pale dry rosé from Provence, France's largest rosé-producing region.

1.1.3.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rosé › Tavel
1.1.3.2.definition: Rhône appellation that makes only rosé.

1.1.3.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rosé › Rosado (Navarra)
1.1.3.3.definition: Spanish rosé tradition of Navarra, typically made from Garnacha.

1.1.3.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rosé › Rosato

1.1.3.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rosé › White Zinfandel
1.1.3.5.definition: Off-dry pink wine from Zinfandel, popularized in California in the 1970s–80s.

1.1.4.definition: Sparkling is a group of 9 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Champagne, Crémant, Cava….

1.1.4.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Champagne
1.1.4.1.definition: Traditional-method sparkling wine from the Champagne AOC in France.

1.1.4.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Crémant
1.1.4.2.definition: French traditional-method sparkling wine made outside Champagne (e.g. Alsace, Loire, Burgundy, Jura).

1.1.4.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Cava
1.1.4.3.definition: Spanish traditional-method sparkling wine (DO Cava), mostly from Catalonia.

1.1.4.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Prosecco
1.1.4.4.definition: Italian sparkling wine from Glera grapes, usually made by the tank method.

1.1.4.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Franciacorta
1.1.4.5.definition: Traditional-method sparkling wine DOCG from Lombardy, Italy. It is made mainly from Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

1.1.4.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Sekt
1.1.4.6.definition: German and Austrian term for sparkling wine.

1.1.4.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Pét-nat (ancestral method)
1.1.4.7.definition: 'Pétillant naturel', a sparkling wine made by the ancestral method.

1.1.4.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Lambrusco
1.1.4.8.definition: Family of red grapes and frizzante wines from Emilia-Romagna.

1.1.4.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Sparkling › Moscato d'Asti
1.1.4.9.definition: Lightly sparkling, sweet, low-alcohol wine from Moscato Bianco grapes in Piedmont.

1.1.5.definition: Orange (Skin-Contact) is a group of 3 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Georgian qvevri (Rkatsiteli), Friulian Ribolla Gialla, Slovenian (Brda) skin-contact.

1.1.5.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Orange (Skin-Contact) › Georgian qvevri (Rkatsiteli)
1.1.5.1.definition: Georgian tradition of fermenting and aging wine, often with skins, in large buried clay vessels (qvevri). It is on UNESCO's intangible-heritage list.

1.1.5.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Orange (Skin-Contact) › Friulian Ribolla Gialla
1.1.5.2.definition: White grape of Friuli and Slovenia (Rebula), often made in skin-contact amber styles.

1.1.5.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Orange (Skin-Contact) › Slovenian (Brda) skin-contact
1.1.5.3.definition: Amber or orange wines from Goriška Brda, Slovenia, made from white grapes macerated on their skins.

1.1.6.definition: Fortified is a group of 6 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Port (Ruby/Tawny/Vintage), Sherry (Fino/Manzanilla/Amontillado/Oloroso/PX), Madeira….

1.1.6.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Fortified › Port (Ruby/Tawny/Vintage)
1.1.6.1.definition: Fortified wine from the Douro Valley, Portugal. Ruby styles keep fresh fruit, Tawny styles are aged oxidatively in wood, and Vintage Port comes from a single declared year.

1.1.6.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Fortified › Sherry (Fino/Manzanilla/Amontillado/Oloroso/PX)
1.1.6.2.definition: Fortified wines from the Jerez area of Andalusia, aged in soleras. Fino and Manzanilla age under flor, Oloroso ages oxidatively, Amontillado does both, and PX is sweet.

1.1.6.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Fortified › Madeira
1.1.6.3.definition: Fortified wine from the Portuguese island of Madeira. It is aged with heat and oxygen, making it very long-lived.

1.1.6.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Fortified › Marsala
1.1.6.4.definition: Fortified wine from western Sicily, made dry to sweet in several aging categories.

1.1.6.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Fortified › Vermouth
1.1.6.5.definition: Aromatized wine flavored with botanicals, traditionally including wormwood.

1.1.6.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Fortified › Vin doux naturel
1.1.6.6.definition: French fortified sweet wine made by mutage (adding spirit during fermentation), e.g. Banyuls.

1.1.7.definition: Dessert is a group of 7 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Sauternes, Tokaji Aszú, Icewine/Eiswein….

1.1.7.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Dessert › Sauternes
1.1.7.1.definition: Sweet white Bordeaux wine from Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc affected by noble rot.

1.1.7.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Dessert › Tokaji Aszú
1.1.7.2.definition: Hungarian sweet wine made by adding botrytized (aszú) berries to base wine or must.

1.1.7.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Dessert › Icewine/Eiswein
1.1.7.3.definition: Sweet wine made from grapes frozen naturally on the vine and pressed while frozen.

1.1.7.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Dessert › Beerenauslese/TBA
1.1.7.4.definition: German/Austrian Prädikat levels for sweet wines from individually selected overripe berries, often affected by noble rot. Trockenbeerenauslese (TBA) uses shriveled, raisined berries and is the sweeter of the two.

1.1.7.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Dessert › Vin Santo
1.1.7.5.definition: Tuscan dessert wine made from dried grapes and aged in small casks (caratelli).

1.1.7.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Dessert › Recioto
1.1.7.6.definition: Sweet wine of the Veneto made from dried grapes (appassimento), e.g. Recioto della Valpolicella.

1.1.7.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Dessert › Late harvest
1.1.7.7.definition: Grapes picked later than normal for higher sugar, used to make sweeter wines.

1.1.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France
1.1.8.definition: France is a group of 10 entries in the Wine Academy, under Non-Testable Red. It includes Tannat, Petit Verdot, Carignan….

1.1.8.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Tannat
1.1.8.1.definition: Very tannic red grape of Madiran, France, and Uruguay's signature grape.

1.1.8.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Petit Verdot
1.1.8.2.definition: Late-ripening red Bordeaux grape, used in small amounts for color and tannin.

1.1.8.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Carignan
1.1.8.3.definition: Late-ripening, high-acid, high-tannin red grape (Cariñena/Mazuelo in Spain). It is common in southern France, Priorat and Sardinia.

1.1.8.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Cinsault
1.1.8.4.definition: Heat-tolerant red grape of southern France, used widely in rosé and light reds. It is a parent of Pinotage.

1.1.8.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Pinot Meunier
1.1.8.5.definition: Red grape related to Pinot Noir, with downy leaves. It is one of Champagne's three main grapes.

1.1.8.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Négrette
1.1.8.6.definition: Red grape of Fronton, southwest France.

1.1.8.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Mondeuse

1.1.8.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Poulsard
1.1.8.8.definition: Pale-skinned red grape of the Jura (also called Ploussard).

1.1.8.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Trousseau
1.1.8.9.definition: Red grape of the Jura, also grown in Portugal as Bastardo.

1.1.8.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › France › Fer Servadou
1.1.8.10.definition: Red grape of southwest France (e.g. Marcillac), also called Mansois or Braucol.

1.1.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy
1.1.9.definition: Italy is a group of 10 entries in the Wine Academy, under Non-Testable Red. It includes Aglianico, Nero d'Avola, Montepulciano….

1.1.9.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Aglianico
1.1.9.1.definition: Tannic southern Italian red grape used for Taurasi and Aglianico del Vulture.

1.1.9.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Nero d'Avola

1.1.9.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Montepulciano
1.1.9.3.definition: Red grape widely planted in central Italy (e.g. Montepulciano d'Abruzzo). It is not related to the Tuscan town of Montepulciano.

1.1.9.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Dolcetto
1.1.9.4.definition: Early-ripening red grape of Piedmont, making soft, fruity reds for early drinking.

1.1.9.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Corvina
1.1.9.5.definition: Main red grape of Valpolicella, Bardolino and Amarone.

1.1.9.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Lagrein
1.1.9.6.definition: Red grape of Alto Adige, Italy.

1.1.9.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Sagrantino
1.1.9.7.definition: Very tannic red grape of Montefalco, Umbria.

1.1.9.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Nerello Mascalese
1.1.9.8.definition: Red grape of Etna, Sicily, making pale, perfumed reds.

1.1.9.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Teroldego

1.1.9.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Italy › Schiava
1.1.9.10.definition: Red grape of Alto Adige (Vernatsch, Trollinger), making light reds.

1.1.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal
1.1.10.definition: Spain & Portugal is a group of 8 entries in the Wine Academy, under Non-Testable Red. It includes Mencía, Bobal, Graciano….

1.1.10.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal › Mencía
1.1.10.1.definition: Red grape of northwest Spain (Bierzo, Ribeira Sacra), identical to Portugal's Jaen.

1.1.10.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal › Bobal
1.1.10.2.definition: Red grape of Utiel-Requena in Valencia, Spain. It is deeply colored and used for reds and rosés.

1.1.10.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal › Graciano
1.1.10.3.definition: Red grape of Rioja, used in small amounts for acidity, color and aroma.

1.1.10.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal › Prieto Picudo

1.1.10.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal › Touriga Nacional
1.1.10.5.definition: Portuguese red grape, a key Port and Douro variety.

1.1.10.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal › Touriga Franca
1.1.10.6.definition: Widely planted Port and Douro red grape.

1.1.10.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal › Baga
1.1.10.7.definition: Thick-skinned, high-acid, tannic red grape of Bairrada, Portugal. It is also used for sparkling wine.

1.1.10.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Spain & Portugal › Castelão
1.1.10.8.definition: Widely planted red grape of southern Portugal, also called Periquita.

1.1.11.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe
1.1.11.definition: Central & Eastern Europe is a group of 9 entries in the Wine Academy, under Non-Testable Red. It includes Blaufränkisch, Zweigelt, St. Laurent….

1.1.11.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › Blaufränkisch
1.1.11.1.definition: Central European red grape, Austria's leading red in Burgenland and called Kékfrankos in Hungary. It typically makes peppery, dark-fruited, fresh reds.

1.1.11.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › Zweigelt
1.1.11.2.definition: Austria's most planted red grape, a cross of Blaufränkisch and St. Laurent.

1.1.11.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › St. Laurent
1.1.11.3.definition: Austrian red grape related to the Pinot family, a parent of Zweigelt.

1.1.11.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › Kadarka
1.1.11.4.definition: Red grape of Hungary and the Balkans, traditionally used in Bikavér.

1.1.11.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › Plavac Mali
1.1.11.5.definition: Croatian red grape of the Dalmatian coast, an offspring of Tribidrag (Zinfandel).

1.1.11.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › Xinomavro
1.1.11.6.definition: High-acid, tannic red grape of Naoussa, northern Greece.

1.1.11.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › Agiorgitiko
1.1.11.7.definition: Red grape of Nemea in the Peloponnese, Greece. It makes soft, fruity reds as well as rosés.

1.1.11.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › Fetească Neagră
1.1.11.8.definition: Indigenous red grape of Romania and Moldova.

1.1.11.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › Central & Eastern Europe › Mavrud
1.1.11.9.definition: Indigenous red grape of Bulgaria (Thracian Valley).

1.1.12.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › New World
1.1.12.definition: New World is a group of 4 entries in the Wine Academy, under Non-Testable Red. It includes Carménère (Chile), País (Chile), Pinotage (South Africa)….

1.1.12.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › New World › Carménère (Chile)
1.1.12.1.definition: Red Bordeaux grape that is now rare in France. It survived in Chile, where it was long mistaken for Merlot until identified in 1994.

1.1.12.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › New World › País (Chile)
1.1.12.2.definition: Historic red grape of Chile, brought by Spanish settlers (Listán Prieto in Spain).

1.1.12.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › New World › Pinotage (South Africa)
1.1.12.3.definition: South African red cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault (then called Hermitage), created in 1925.

1.1.12.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable Red › New World › Bonarda (Argentina)
1.1.12.4.definition: Argentina's widely planted red Bonarda, identified as Douce Noir (Corbeau) from Savoie. It is not the same as Italian Bonarda.

1.1.13.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France
1.1.13.definition: France is a group of 10 entries in the Wine Academy, under Non-Testable White. It includes Marsanne, Roussanne, Melon de Bourgogne….

1.1.13.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Marsanne
1.1.13.1.definition: White grape of the northern Rhône (Hermitage, Saint-Joseph), often blended with Roussanne.

1.1.13.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Roussanne
1.1.13.2.definition: Aromatic white grape of the northern Rhône, often blended with Marsanne.

1.1.13.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Melon de Bourgogne
1.1.13.3.definition: White grape of Muscadet in the western Loire, often aged on its lees (sur lie).

1.1.13.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Aligoté
1.1.13.4.definition: White grape of Burgundy, typically high in acidity. It is used for Bourgogne Aligoté and, traditionally, for the Kir cocktail.

1.1.13.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Petit Manseng
1.1.13.5.definition: White grape of Jurançon with small, thick-skinned berries, used for sweet and dry wines.

1.1.13.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Gros Manseng
1.1.13.6.definition: White grape of southwest France (Jurançon, Gascony), used for dry and sweet wines.

1.1.13.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Savagnin
1.1.13.7.definition: Jura white grape used for Vin Jaune. It is the same variety as Traminer.

1.1.13.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Picpoul
1.1.13.8.definition: Grape of the Languedoc, best known for high-acid Picpoul de Pinet whites.

1.1.13.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Clairette
1.1.13.9.definition: White grape of southern France, used for Clairette de Die sparkling wine and in Rhône blends.

1.1.13.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › France › Mauzac
1.1.13.10.definition: White grape of Gaillac and Limoux, used in Blanquette de Limoux.

1.1.14.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › Italy
1.1.14.definition: Italy is a group of 10 entries in the Wine Academy, under Non-Testable White. It includes Garganega, Vermentino, Fiano….

1.1.14.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › Italy › Garganega
1.1.14.1.definition: Main white grape of Soave, Veneto.

1.1.14.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › Italy › Vermentino
1.1.14.2.definition: White grape of Sardinia, Liguria and Provence (Rolle).

1.1.14.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Non-Testable White › Italy › Fiano

1.1.29.1.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. rupestris cross. It is vigorous and drought-tolerant, widely used in dry Mediterranean vineyards.

1.1.29.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Berlandieri × Rupestris › 1103 Paulsen
1.1.29.2.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. rupestris cross, bred in Sicily. It is vigorous and tolerates drought and moderate salinity.

1.1.29.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Berlandieri × Rupestris › 140 Ruggeri
1.1.29.3.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. rupestris cross, bred in Sicily. It is very vigorous and tolerates drought and limestone soils.

1.1.29.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Berlandieri × Rupestris › 99 Richter
1.1.29.4.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. rupestris cross. Vigorous and drought-tolerant, used in warm regions.

1.1.30.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Nematode-Resistant & Other
1.1.30.definition: Nematode-Resistant & Other is a group of 6 entries in the Wine Academy, under Rootstocks. It includes Freedom, Harmony, Dog Ridge….

1.1.30.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Nematode-Resistant & Other › Freedom
1.1.30.1.definition: Nematode-resistant rootstock with Vitis champinii in its parentage, used in California.

1.1.30.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Nematode-Resistant & Other › Harmony

1.1.30.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Nematode-Resistant & Other › Dog Ridge
1.1.30.3.definition: Vigorous rootstock selection of Vitis champinii, tolerant of nematodes and drought.

1.1.30.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Nematode-Resistant & Other › Ramsey (Salt Creek)
1.1.30.4.definition: Very vigorous Vitis champinii rootstock, tolerant of nematodes, drought and salinity.

1.1.30.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Nematode-Resistant & Other › 1616 Couderc
1.1.30.5.definition: Rootstock bred in France from a Vitis solonis × V. riparia cross. It is low-vigor and tolerates wet and somewhat saline soils.

1.1.30.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Rootstocks › Nematode-Resistant & Other › Own-rooted (ungrafted)
1.1.30.6.definition: A vine growing on its own roots rather than grafted onto a rootstock.

1.1.31.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems
1.1.31.definition: Training Systems is a group of 11 entries in the Wine Academy, under Canopy Management. It includes Single Guyot, Double Guyot, Bilateral cordon (spur-pruned)….

1.1.31.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Single Guyot
1.1.31.1.definition: Cane-pruning system that keeps one cane plus a renewal spur.

1.1.31.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Double Guyot
1.1.31.2.definition: Cane-pruning system that keeps two canes, one trained each way along the wire.

1.1.31.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Bilateral cordon (spur-pruned)
1.1.31.3.definition: Vine training in which a permanent arm (cordon) extends in two directions along a wire. Short spurs on the cordon are pruned each winter.

1.1.31.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Vertical shoot positioning (VSP)
1.1.31.4.definition: Trellis system where shoots are trained upward in a narrow vertical curtain.

1.1.31.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Gobelet (bush vine)
1.1.31.5.definition: Free-standing vine trained without wires into a goblet shape, common in hot, dry regions.

1.1.31.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Pergola
1.1.31.6.definition: Overhead trellis system, traditional in parts of Italy and northwest Spain.

1.1.31.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Lyre
1.1.31.7.definition: Divided-canopy trellis shaped like a U or lyre.

1.1.31.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Scott Henry
1.1.31.8.definition: Divided vertical trellis with upper shoots trained up and lower shoots trained down.

1.1.31.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Smart-Dyson
1.1.31.9.definition: Divided vertical trellis with upward and downward shoots, devised by Richard Smart and John Dyson.

1.1.31.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Geneva Double Curtain
1.1.31.10.definition: Divided-canopy trellis developed at Geneva, New York, with two hanging curtains of shoots.

1.1.31.11.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Training Systems › Sprawl
1.1.31.11.definition: Training with little shoot positioning, letting the canopy hang freely.

1.1.32.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices
1.1.32.definition: Canopy Practices is a group of 8 entries in the Wine Academy, under Canopy Management. It includes Cane pruning, Spur pruning, Shoot thinning….

1.1.32.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices › Cane pruning
1.1.32.1.definition: Winter pruning that keeps one or two of last year's canes and ties them along the wire to bear the new crop. The Guyot system is an example.

1.1.32.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices › Spur pruning
1.1.32.2.definition: Winter pruning of last year's canes down to short spurs on a permanent cordon.

1.1.32.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices › Shoot thinning
1.1.32.3.definition: Removing excess or poorly placed shoots early in the season.

1.1.32.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices › Shoot positioning
1.1.32.4.definition: Training the season's new shoots into place on the trellis.

1.1.32.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices › Leaf removal
1.1.32.5.definition: Removing leaves around the grape clusters to improve air flow and sun exposure.

1.1.32.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices › Hedging (topping)
1.1.32.6.definition: Trimming the tops and sides of the vine canopy during the growing season.

1.1.32.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices › Green harvest (crop thinning)
1.1.32.7.definition: Removing some unripe bunches to reduce yield and concentrate the rest.

1.1.32.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Canopy Management › Canopy Practices › Cover crops
1.1.32.8.definition: Plants grown between vine rows to manage soil erosion, structure, water and vine vigor.

1.1.33.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking
1.1.33.definition: Red Winemaking is a group of 10 entries in the Wine Academy, under Winemaking Techniques. It includes Destemming, Whole-cluster fermentation, Cold soak….

1.1.33.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Destemming
1.1.33.1.definition: Separating grape berries from their stems before crushing or fermentation.

1.1.33.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Whole-cluster fermentation
1.1.33.2.definition: Fermenting red grapes with their stems still attached.

1.1.33.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Cold soak
1.1.33.3.definition: Holding crushed red grapes cold before fermentation to extract color and aroma.

1.1.33.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Carbonic maceration
1.1.33.4.definition: Whole, uncrushed grapes ferment inside a CO2-filled vessel, giving fruity, low-tannin reds (as in Beaujolais).

1.1.33.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Pump-over (remontage)
1.1.33.5.definition: Pumping fermenting red wine from the bottom of the tank over the skin cap to extract color and tannin.

1.1.33.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Punch-down (pigeage)
1.1.33.6.definition: Pushing the floating skin cap down into fermenting red wine to extract color and tannin.

1.1.33.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Délestage (rack & return)
1.1.33.7.definition: Draining fermenting red juice off the skins into another tank, then pouring it back over the cap to extract gently.

1.1.33.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Extended maceration
1.1.33.8.definition: Leaving red wine on its skins after fermentation ends to change tannin texture.

1.1.33.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Saignée
1.1.33.9.definition: Bleeding off juice from a red-wine tank early to make rosé and concentrate the remaining red.

1.1.33.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Red Winemaking › Malolactic conversion
1.1.33.10.definition: Bacterial conversion of malic acid into lactic acid, softening a wine's acidity.

1.1.34.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking
1.1.34.definition: White & Rosé Winemaking is a group of 8 entries in the Wine Academy, under Winemaking Techniques. It includes Whole-bunch pressing, Skin contact, Cold settling (débourbage)….

1.1.34.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking › Whole-bunch pressing
1.1.34.1.definition: Pressing whole clusters without crushing, giving cleaner, lower-phenolic juice.

1.1.34.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking › Skin contact
1.1.34.2.definition: Leaving juice in contact with grape skins; for white grapes this makes 'orange' or amber wine.

1.1.34.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking › Cold settling (débourbage)
1.1.34.3.definition: Letting freshly pressed white juice rest cold so solids settle out before fermentation.

1.1.34.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking › Cool fermentation
1.1.34.4.definition: Fermenting at low temperatures (often around 10–16 °C for whites) to keep fresh, fruity aromas.

1.1.34.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking › Lees aging (sur lie)
1.1.34.5.definition: Leaving wine in contact with its spent yeast after fermentation to build texture and flavor.

1.1.34.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking › Bâtonnage
1.1.34.6.definition: Stirring the lees (spent yeast) back into a wine during aging to add texture.

1.1.34.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking › Direct-press rosé
1.1.34.7.definition: Rosé made by pressing red grapes right away, giving brief skin contact and pale color.

1.1.34.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › White & Rosé Winemaking › Blocked malolactic
1.1.34.8.definition: Preventing malolactic fermentation (for example by cold, sulfur dioxide or filtration) so the wine keeps its sharper malic acidity.

1.1.35.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods
1.1.35.definition: Sparkling Methods is a group of 8 entries in the Wine Academy, under Winemaking Techniques. It includes Traditional method, Tank (Charmat) method, Ancestral method….

1.1.35.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods › Traditional method
1.1.35.1.definition: Sparkling method in which the second fermentation happens in the bottle sold (as in Champagne and Cava).

1.1.35.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods › Tank (Charmat) method
1.1.35.2.definition: Sparkling method with the second fermentation in a pressurized tank (common for Prosecco).

1.1.35.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods › Ancestral method
1.1.35.3.definition: Sparkling method where wine is bottled before primary fermentation finishes, trapping its CO2.

1.1.35.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods › Transfer method
1.1.35.4.definition: Sparkling method with second fermentation in bottle, after which the wine is transferred to a tank, filtered and rebottled.

1.1.35.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods › Riddling (remuage)
1.1.35.5.definition: Gradually turning and tilting sparkling-wine bottles so sediment collects in the neck before disgorgement.

1.1.35.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods › Disgorgement
1.1.35.6.definition: Removing the frozen plug of yeast sediment from a traditional-method sparkling wine bottle.

1.1.35.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods › Dosage
1.1.35.7.definition: Sugar-and-wine mixture added after disgorgement, setting a sparkling wine's sweetness level.

1.1.35.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Sparkling Methods › Carbonation
1.1.35.8.definition: Presence of dissolved CO2, which makes wine sparkling. It comes either from a second fermentation or from injected gas.

1.1.36.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Fortified & Oxidative
1.1.36.definition: Fortified & Oxidative is a group of 5 entries in the Wine Academy, under Winemaking Techniques. It includes Mutage (fortification during fermentation), Post-fermentation fortification, Flor (biological aging)….

1.1.36.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Fortified & Oxidative › Mutage (fortification during fermentation)
1.1.36.1.definition: Stopping fermentation by adding grape spirit, leaving natural sugar (used for Port and vins doux naturels).

1.1.36.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Fortified & Oxidative › Post-fermentation fortification
1.1.36.2.definition: Adding spirit after fermentation has finished, leaving a dry base that may be sweetened later. Sherry is the classic example.

1.1.36.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Fortified & Oxidative › Flor (biological aging)
1.1.36.3.definition: A layer of yeast on the surface of Fino and Manzanilla Sherry that protects the wine from oxidation.

1.1.36.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Fortified & Oxidative › Oxidative aging
1.1.36.4.definition: Aging with deliberate oxygen contact, giving nutty, dried-fruit flavors (e.g. Oloroso, tawny Port).

1.1.36.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Fortified & Oxidative › Estufagem (Madeira)
1.1.36.5.definition: Madeira method of heating wine in tanks (estufas) to speed up aging.

1.1.37.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Finishing
1.1.37.definition: Finishing is a group of 4 entries in the Wine Academy, under Winemaking Techniques. It includes Fining, Filtration, Cold stabilization….

1.1.37.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Finishing › Fining
1.1.37.1.definition: Adding an agent (such as bentonite or egg white) that binds and removes haze or harsh compounds.

1.1.37.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Finishing › Filtration
1.1.37.2.definition: Passing wine through a filter medium to remove yeast, bacteria or haze before bottling.

1.1.37.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Finishing › Cold stabilization
1.1.37.3.definition: Chilling wine so tartrate crystals form and can be removed before bottling.

1.1.37.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Winemaking Techniques › Finishing › Blending
1.1.37.4.definition: Combining wines from different grapes, vineyards, vessels or vintages to build balance and a consistent style.

1.1.38.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods
1.1.38.definition: Oak & Other Woods is a group of 10 entries in the Wine Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes American white oak (Quercus alba), French sessile oak (Q. petraea), French pedunculate oak (Q. robur)….

1.1.38.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › American white oak (Quercus alba)
1.1.38.1.definition: The main American barrel oak. Its staves are usually sawn rather than split, and it typically gives stronger vanilla and coconut notes than French oak.

1.1.38.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › French sessile oak (Q. petraea)
1.1.38.2.definition: European oak species with tighter grain and more aromatic compounds, widely preferred for wine barrels.

1.1.38.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › French pedunculate oak (Q. robur)
1.1.38.3.definition: European oak species, more porous and higher in tannin than sessile oak. It is traditionally preferred for spirits such as Cognac.

1.1.38.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › Hungarian oak (Q. petraea)
1.1.38.4.definition: Sessile oak from Hungary's forests (e.g. Zemplén), used for barrels.

1.1.38.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › Oregon oak (Q. garryana)
1.1.38.5.definition: Oak native to the Pacific Northwest, sometimes used for wine barrels.

1.1.38.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › Mizunara (Q. mongolica, Japan)
1.1.38.6.definition: Japanese oak used for whisky casks. It is porous and hard to work, and is associated with sandalwood and incense aromas.

1.1.38.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › Acacia (black locust)
1.1.38.7.definition: Wood of the black locust tree (Robinia pseudoacacia), sometimes used for white-wine barrels. It is commonly described as giving floral notes with little oak-style spice.

1.1.38.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › Chestnut (Castanea sativa)
1.1.38.8.definition: Sweet chestnut wood, historically used for barrels in Italy and France. It is porous and low in aromatic compounds, so it allows oxygen exchange.

1.1.38.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › Cherry (Prunus avium)
1.1.38.9.definition: Cherry wood, occasionally used for casks. It is commonly described as oxidizing wine faster and adding fruity, lightly sweet notes.

1.1.38.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Oak & Other Woods › Amburana (Brazil)
1.1.38.10.definition: Brazilian hardwood (Amburana cearensis) used for casks, especially for cachaça. It gives strong sweet-spice aromas often compared to cinnamon.

1.1.39.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › French Oak Forests
1.1.39.definition: French Oak Forests is a group of 7 entries in the Wine Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes Allier, Tronçais (Allier), Nevers….

1.1.39.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › French Oak Forests › Allier
1.1.39.1.definition: French département whose forests (including Tronçais) supply tight-grained sessile oak prized for wine barrels.

1.1.39.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › French Oak Forests › Tronçais (Allier)
1.1.39.2.definition: Famous oak forest in the Allier, France, planted under Colbert, with tight-grained oak.

1.1.39.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › French Oak Forests › Nevers
1.1.39.3.definition: Oak forests of the Nièvre, France, known for fine-grained oak.

1.1.39.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › French Oak Forests › Bertranges
1.1.39.4.definition: Oak forest in the Nièvre, France, known for fine-grained sessile oak for barrels.

1.1.39.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › French Oak Forests › Vosges
1.1.39.5.definition: Oak forests of the Vosges mountains, France, used for barrels.

1.1.39.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › French Oak Forests › Limousin (wide grain, Cognac)
1.1.39.6.definition: Oak forests near Limoges, France, with wide-grained, tannic oak traditionally used for Cognac.

1.1.39.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › French Oak Forests › Jupilles
1.1.39.7.definition: Oak forest in the Sarthe, France, used for barrels.

1.1.40.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Seasoning
1.1.40.definition: Seasoning is a group of 3 entries in the Wine Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes Open-air seasoning (typically 24–36 months), Kiln-dried staves, Rain & sun leaching of harsh tannins.

1.1.40.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Seasoning › Open-air seasoning (typically 24–36 months)
1.1.40.1.definition: Drying barrel staves outdoors so rain and sun leach harsh tannins before coopering.

1.1.40.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Seasoning › Kiln-dried staves
1.1.40.2.definition: Barrel staves dried quickly in kilns rather than seasoned outdoors.

1.1.40.3.term: Rain & sun leaching of harsh tannins
1.1.40.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Seasoning › Rain & sun leaching of harsh tannins
1.1.40.3.definition: The effect of outdoor seasoning on staves: weather washes out bitter tannins and starts breaking down wood compounds.

1.1.41.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Toast Levels
1.1.41.definition: Toast Levels is a group of 7 entries in the Wine Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes Light toast, Medium toast, Medium-plus toast….

1.1.41.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Toast Levels › Light toast
1.1.41.1.definition: Barrel interior toasted briefly, keeping fresh wood character and less roasted flavor.

1.1.41.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Toast Levels › Medium toast
1.1.41.2.definition: Middle toast level for barrels, balancing fresh oak with vanilla and toasty notes.

1.1.41.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Toast Levels › Medium-plus toast
1.1.41.3.definition: Toast level between medium and heavy, giving more caramel and spice.

1.1.41.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Toast Levels › Heavy toast
1.1.41.4.definition: Barrel interior toasted long and hot, giving roasted, smoky, coffee-like flavors.

1.1.41.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Toast Levels › Toasted heads
1.1.41.5.definition: Barrel ends (heads) toasted like the staves, adding more toast flavor.

1.1.41.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Toast Levels › Untoasted heads
1.1.41.6.definition: Barrel heads left untoasted, keeping more raw-wood character.

1.1.41.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Toast Levels › See Spirits Academy: char levels
1.1.41.7.definition: Cross-reference: barrel char levels (#1–#4) are covered in the Spirits Academy.

1.1.42.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes
1.1.42.definition: Barrel Sizes is a group of 10 entries in the Wine Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes Blood tub (~40 L), Quarter cask (~125 L), American standard barrel (200 L / 53 gal)….

1.1.42.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Blood tub (~40 L)
1.1.42.1.definition: Very small cask of about 40 litres. Its high wood-to-liquid ratio speeds wood extraction.

1.1.42.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Quarter cask (~125 L)
1.1.42.2.definition: Small cask that speeds up spirit maturation.

1.1.42.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › American standard barrel (200 L / 53 gal)
1.1.42.3.definition: The common 53-gallon (~200 L) American oak barrel.

1.1.42.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Bordeaux barrique (225 L)

1.1.42.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Burgundy pièce (228 L)

1.1.42.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Hogshead (~250 L)
1.1.42.6.definition: Cask of around 250 L, often rebuilt from bourbon barrels.

1.1.42.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Puncheon (~450–500 L)
1.1.42.7.definition: Large cask used for wine, rum and whisky.

1.1.42.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Sherry butt (~500 L)
1.1.42.8.definition: Traditional Sherry cask of around 500 L, often reused to age whisky.

1.1.42.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Port pipe (~550–650 L)

1.1.42.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel Sizes › Foudre / foeder (1,000 L+)

1.1.43.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › New vs Used
1.1.43.definition: New vs Used is a group of 6 entries in the Wine Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes New oak, First fill, Refill (second fill+)….

1.1.43.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › New vs Used › New oak
1.1.43.1.definition: A barrel used for the first time, giving the most oak flavor and tannin.

1.1.43.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › New vs Used › First fill
1.1.43.2.definition: A cask used for the first time after its previous contents (e.g. first-fill ex-bourbon), giving more flavor than refill casks.

1.1.43.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › New vs Used › Refill (second fill+)
1.1.43.3.definition: A cask reused after its first fill, giving less flavor each time.

1.1.43.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › New vs Used › Neutral oak (3+ uses)
1.1.43.4.definition: Barrels used several times that now give little oak flavor but still allow slow oxygen exchange.

1.1.43.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › New vs Used › Rejuvenated (re-toasted/re-charred)
1.1.43.5.definition: A used cask that has been scraped and re-toasted or re-charred to restore some of its flavor.

1.1.43.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › New vs Used › Percentage new oak (wine élevage)
