1.2.38.3.definition: Traditional British two-row barley variety prized for pale ale malt.

1.2.38.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Vienna malt
1.2.38.4.definition: Lightly kilned malt with a toasty, malty character, used in Vienna lager and Märzen.

1.2.38.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Munich malt
1.2.38.5.definition: Kilned base malt that is darker than pilsner malt and gives a rich, bready flavor.

1.2.38.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Wheat malt
1.2.38.6.definition: Malted wheat, which adds protein for body and head retention.

1.2.38.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Rye malt
1.2.38.7.definition: Malted rye, adding spicy flavor; it can make the mash sticky.

1.2.38.8.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Crystal/caramel malts
1.2.38.8.definition: Malts stewed to crystallize sugars inside the grain, adding sweetness, body and caramel color.

1.2.38.9.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Chocolate malt
1.2.38.9.definition: Dark roasted malt that gives chocolate and coffee flavors.

1.2.38.10.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Black (patent) malt
1.2.38.10.definition: Very dark malt roasted at high temperature, used for color and sharp roast flavor.

1.2.38.11.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Roasted barley
1.2.38.11.definition: Unmalted barley roasted dark, giving the dry, coffee-like flavor of Irish stout.

1.2.38.12.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Smoked malt
1.2.38.12.definition: Malt dried over smoke (beechwood for Rauchbier, peat for some Scotch-style beers).

1.2.38.13.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Malts › Acidulated malt
1.2.38.13.definition: Malt coated with lactic acid, used in small amounts to lower mash pH (common under the German Reinheitsgebot).

1.2.39.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere
1.2.39.definition: Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere is a group of 10 entries in the Beer Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Cascade, Centennial, Citra….

1.2.39.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Cascade
1.2.39.1.definition: US hop released in 1972 with grapefruit and floral aroma; defined American Pale Ale.

1.2.39.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Centennial
1.2.39.2.definition: US hop with floral and citrus character, sometimes called a 'super Cascade'.

1.2.39.3.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Citra
1.2.39.3.definition: US aroma hop released in 2007, with strong tropical-fruit and citrus aroma.

1.2.39.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Mosaic
1.2.39.4.definition: US aroma hop with blueberry, tropical and pine notes.

1.2.39.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Simcoe
1.2.39.5.definition: US hop with pine and passion-fruit character.

1.2.39.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Amarillo
1.2.39.6.definition: US aroma hop with orange and citrus character.

1.2.39.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Chinook
1.2.39.7.definition: US dual-purpose hop with pine, resin and grapefruit character.

1.2.39.8.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Galaxy (Australia)
1.2.39.8.definition: Australian aroma hop with intense passion-fruit and citrus aroma.

1.2.39.9.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Nelson Sauvin (NZ)
1.2.39.9.definition: New Zealand hop known for white-wine and gooseberry aromas.

1.2.39.10.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: US & Southern Hemisphere › Motueka (NZ)
1.2.39.10.definition: New Zealand aroma hop with lime and citrus character.

1.2.40.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: European
1.2.40.definition: Hops: European is a group of 7 entries in the Beer Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Saaz, Hallertauer Mittelfrüh, Tettnanger….

1.2.40.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: European › Saaz
1.2.40.1.definition: Czech noble hop with mild, spicy aroma, classic in Czech pale lagers.

1.2.40.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: European › Hallertauer Mittelfrüh
1.2.40.2.definition: Traditional German noble hop from the Hallertau, with mild floral-spicy aroma.

1.2.40.3.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: European › Tettnanger
1.2.40.3.definition: German noble aroma hop from Tettnang.

1.2.40.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: European › Spalter
1.2.40.4.definition: German noble-type aroma hop from Spalt, with mild, spicy aroma.

1.2.40.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: European › East Kent Goldings
1.2.40.5.definition: Classic English aroma hop with soft, earthy, honeyed character.

1.2.40.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: European › Fuggle
1.2.40.6.definition: Traditional English aroma hop with earthy, woody character.

1.2.40.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hops: European › Styrian Golding
1.2.40.7.definition: Slovenian hop, genetically Fuggle-derived, with earthy, spicy aroma.

1.2.41.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes
1.2.41.definition: Yeast & Microbes is a group of 8 entries in the Beer Academy, under Science. It includes Ale yeast (S. cerevisiae), Lager yeast (S. pastorianus), Kveik….

1.2.41.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes › Ale yeast (S. cerevisiae)
1.2.41.1.definition: Top-fermenting yeast working at warmer temperatures, often producing fruity esters.

1.2.41.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes › Lager yeast (S. pastorianus)
1.2.41.2.definition: Bottom-fermenting yeast that works at cool temperatures and gives clean flavors.

1.2.41.3.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes › Kveik
1.2.41.3.definition: Traditional Norwegian farmhouse ale yeasts that ferment cleanly at unusually high temperatures.

1.2.41.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes › Belgian/Saison yeast
1.2.41.4.definition: Ale yeast strains that give spicy, peppery and fruity character and often ferment very dry.

1.2.41.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes › Hefeweizen yeast
1.2.41.5.definition: Weizen ale yeast that produces banana-like (isoamyl acetate) and clove-like (4-vinyl guaiacol) aromas.

1.2.41.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes › Brettanomyces
1.2.41.6.definition: Wild yeast genus giving 'funky', earthy or fruity flavors; prized in some beers, a fault in most wines.

1.2.41.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes › Lactobacillus
1.2.41.7.definition: Lactic acid bacteria used to sour beers such as Berliner Weisse and Gose.

1.2.41.8.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Yeast & Microbes › Pediococcus
1.2.41.8.definition: Lactic acid bacteria used in sour beers such as lambic; it can produce diacetyl.

1.2.42.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles
1.2.42.definition: Water Profiles is a group of 8 entries in the Beer Academy, under Science. It includes Burton-on-Trent (high sulfate), Pilsen (very soft), Munich (carbonate)….

1.2.42.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles › Burton-on-Trent (high sulfate)
1.2.42.1.definition: English brewing town whose hard, sulfate-rich water accentuates hop bitterness in pale ales.

1.2.42.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles › Pilsen (very soft)
1.2.42.2.definition: Plzeň's very soft, low-mineral water, key to Czech pale lager.

1.2.42.3.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles › Munich (carbonate)
1.2.42.3.definition: Munich's carbonate-rich water suits dark, malty lagers such as Dunkel.

1.2.42.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles › Dublin (carbonate)
1.2.42.4.definition: Dublin's water is high in carbonate, which suits dark, roasty beers such as stout.

1.2.42.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles › London
1.2.42.5.definition: London's water is high in carbonate, historically suited to porters and brown beers.

1.2.42.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles › Dortmund
1.2.42.6.definition: German brewing city with moderately hard water, associated with the Dortmunder Export style.

1.2.42.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles › Vienna
1.2.42.7.definition: Vienna's water, associated with the Vienna lager style.

1.2.42.8.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Water Profiles › Sulfate-to-chloride ratio
1.2.42.8.definition: Brewing-water balance: more sulfate sharpens hop bitterness, more chloride emphasizes malt fullness.

1.2.43.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process
1.2.43.definition: Brewing Process is a group of 11 entries in the Beer Academy, under Production. It includes Malting (steep, germinate, kiln), Milling, Mashing….

1.2.43.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Malting (steep, germinate, kiln)
1.2.43.1.definition: Turning grain into malt by soaking it, letting it sprout, then drying it in a kiln to develop enzymes and flavor.

1.2.43.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Milling
1.2.43.2.definition: Crushing malt to expose the starch while keeping husks intact for lautering.

1.2.43.3.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Mashing
1.2.43.3.definition: Steeping crushed malt in hot water so enzymes convert starch into fermentable sugars.

1.2.43.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Lautering
1.2.43.4.definition: Separating the sweet wort from spent grain after mashing.

1.2.43.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Sparging
1.2.43.5.definition: Rinsing the grain bed with hot water to collect remaining sugars.

1.2.43.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Boil
1.2.43.6.definition: Boiling the wort to sterilize it, isomerize hop acids and drive off unwanted compounds.

1.2.43.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Whirlpool
1.2.43.7.definition: Swirling hot wort after the boil to collect solids in the center; hops added here give aroma.

1.2.43.8.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Wort chilling
1.2.43.8.definition: Rapidly cooling boiled wort to fermentation temperature.

1.2.43.9.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Fermentation
1.2.43.9.definition: Yeast converting wort sugars into alcohol and CO2, also producing flavor compounds.

1.2.43.10.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Lagering/conditioning
1.2.43.10.definition: Cold maturation of beer after fermentation to clarify and smooth it.

1.2.43.11.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Packaging
1.2.43.11.definition: Putting finished beer into bottles, cans or kegs while limiting oxygen pickup.

1.2.44.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods
1.2.44.definition: Mash Methods is a group of 8 entries in the Beer Academy, under Techniques. It includes Single infusion, Step infusion, Single decoction….

1.2.44.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods › Single infusion
1.2.44.1.definition: Mash held at one temperature rest.

1.2.44.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods › Step infusion
1.2.44.2.definition: Mash raised through several temperature rests by heating or by adding hot water.

1.2.44.3.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods › Single decoction
1.2.44.3.definition: Mash method in which part of the mash is boiled once and returned to raise the temperature.

1.2.44.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods › Double decoction
1.2.44.4.definition: Mash method in which part of the mash is boiled and returned twice to raise the temperature.

1.2.44.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods › Triple decoction
1.2.44.5.definition: Mash method in which part of the mash is boiled and returned three times to step up temperature.

1.2.44.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods › Cereal mash
1.2.44.6.definition: Cooking unmalted grains such as corn or rice so their starch can be converted in the mash.

1.2.44.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods › Protein rest
1.2.44.7.definition: Mash rest at about 45–55 °C, meant to break down proteins; with modern well-modified malts it is often skipped.

1.2.44.8.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Mash Methods › Saccharification rest
1.2.44.8.definition: Mash rest at about 62–72 °C, where amylase enzymes convert starch into sugars.

1.2.45.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Hopping Techniques
1.2.45.definition: Hopping Techniques is a group of 7 entries in the Beer Academy, under Techniques. It includes Bittering addition, Flavor/aroma addition, Whirlpool hop stand….

1.2.45.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Hopping Techniques › Bittering addition
1.2.45.1.definition: Hops added early in the boil, so alpha acids isomerize and give bitterness.

1.2.45.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Hopping Techniques › Flavor/aroma addition
1.2.45.2.definition: Hops added late in the boil, or after it, to keep their volatile aromas.

1.2.45.3.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Hopping Techniques › Whirlpool hop stand
1.2.45.3.definition: Hops steeped in hot wort after the boil, below boiling, to extract aroma.

1.2.45.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Hopping Techniques › Dry hopping
1.2.45.4.definition: Adding hops after the boil, usually during or after fermentation, for aroma without much bitterness.

1.2.45.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Hopping Techniques › Biotransformation
1.2.45.5.definition: Chemical changes to hop aroma compounds caused by active yeast, e.g. when dry hopping during fermentation.

1.2.45.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Hopping Techniques › First wort hopping
1.2.45.6.definition: Adding hops to the kettle as the wort is collected, before the boil.

1.2.45.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Techniques › Hopping Techniques › CO2 hop extract
1.2.45.7.definition: Hop resins extracted with supercritical CO2, used for consistent bittering.

1.2.46.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements
1.2.46.definition: Measurements is a group of 8 entries in the Beer Academy, under Science. It includes Original gravity (OG), Final gravity (FG), ABV….

1.2.46.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements › Original gravity (OG)
1.2.46.1.definition: Density of wort before fermentation, indicating its sugar content.

1.2.46.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements › Final gravity (FG)
1.2.46.2.definition: Density of beer after fermentation; the drop from OG shows how much sugar was fermented.

1.2.46.3.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements › ABV
1.2.46.3.definition: Alcohol by volume: the percentage of a drink's volume that is ethanol.

1.2.46.4.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements › IBU
1.2.46.4.definition: International Bitterness Units, a lab measure of iso-alpha acids that indicates beer bitterness.

1.2.46.5.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements › SRM color
1.2.46.5.definition: Standard Reference Method, the US scale for beer color.

1.2.46.6.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements › EBC color
1.2.46.6.definition: European Brewery Convention scale for beer and malt color.

1.2.46.7.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements › Apparent attenuation
1.2.46.7.definition: Percentage of the original gravity consumed by fermentation, as measured by a hydrometer.

1.2.46.8.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Science › Measurements › Degrees Plato
1.2.46.8.definition: Measure of wort or beer density expressed as percent sugar by weight.

1.2.47.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Aging Requirements › Aging Requirements
1.2.47.definition: Aging Requirements is a group of 2 entries in the Beer Academy, under Aging Requirements. It includes No legal aging minimums for beer, BJCP is a style guide, not law.
facts: US/EU beer style names (including barrel-aged styles) carry no legally mandated aging periods; BJCP and brewery trade guides are voluntary style references, not statute [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.2.47.1.term: No legal aging minimums for beer
1.2.47.1.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Aging Requirements › Aging Requirements › No legal aging minimums for beer
1.2.47.1.definition: No legal aging minimums for beer.
facts: US/EU beer style names (including barrel-aged styles) carry no legally mandated aging periods; BJCP and brewery trade guides are voluntary style references, not statute [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.2.47.2.term: BJCP is a style guide, not law
1.2.47.2.path: Cask Guild › Beer Academy › Aging Requirements › Aging Requirements › BJCP is a style guide, not law
1.2.47.2.definition: BJCP is a style guide, not law.
facts: US/EU beer style names (including barrel-aged styles) carry no legally mandated aging periods; BJCP and brewery trade guides are voluntary style references, not statute [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey
1.3.1.definition: American Whiskey is a group of 8 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Bourbon, Straight Bourbon, Bottled-in-Bond….

1.3.1.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey › Bourbon
1.3.1.1.definition: US whiskey made from at least 51% corn and aged in new charred oak containers.

1.3.1.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey › Straight Bourbon
1.3.1.2.definition: Bourbon aged at least 2 years in new charred oak with no added coloring or flavoring.

1.3.1.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey › Bottled-in-Bond
1.3.1.3.definition: US designation: one distiller, one season, aged at least 4 years in a bonded warehouse, bottled at 100 proof.

1.3.1.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey › Tennessee Whiskey
1.3.1.4.definition: Whiskey made in Tennessee meeting bourbon rules; most is filtered through maple charcoal (Lincoln County Process).

1.3.1.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey › Rye Whiskey
1.3.1.5.definition: US whiskey made from at least 51% rye and aged in new charred oak.

1.3.1.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey › Wheat Whiskey
1.3.1.6.definition: US whiskey made from at least 51% wheat.

1.3.1.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey › Corn Whiskey
1.3.1.7.definition: US whiskey from at least 80% corn. If aged, it must be in used or uncharred new oak.

1.3.1.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › American Whiskey › American Single Malt
1.3.1.8.definition: US whiskey made from 100% malted barley at one distillery. The TTB recognized it as a formal category in 2024.

1.3.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky
1.3.2.definition: Scotch Whisky is a group of 10 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Speyside, Highland, Lowland….

1.3.2.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Speyside
1.3.2.1.definition: Scotch whisky region along the River Spey, with the most distilleries.

1.3.2.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Highland
1.3.2.2.definition: The largest Scotch whisky region by area.

1.3.2.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Lowland
1.3.2.3.definition: Scotch whisky region in southern Scotland, historically triple-distilled.

1.3.2.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Islay
1.3.2.4.definition: Scotch whisky region on the island of Islay, known for peated malts.

1.3.2.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Campbeltown
1.3.2.5.definition: Scotch whisky region on the Kintyre peninsula.

1.3.2.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Islands (Highland sub-region)
1.3.2.6.definition: Scotch whiskies from the islands other than Islay (e.g. Skye, Orkney, Mull, Jura, Arran), grouped under the Highland region.

1.3.2.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Single Malt
1.3.2.7.definition: Malt whisky from 100% malted barley produced at a single distillery.

1.3.2.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Blended Malt
1.3.2.8.definition: Blend of single malts from more than one distillery, with no grain whisky.

1.3.2.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Single Grain
1.3.2.9.definition: Grain whisky from a single distillery.

1.3.2.10.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Scotch Whisky › Blended Scotch
1.3.2.10.definition: Blend of malt and grain Scotch whiskies.

1.3.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Irish Whiskey
1.3.3.definition: Irish Whiskey is a group of 4 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Single Pot Still, Single Malt, Single Grain….

1.3.3.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Irish Whiskey › Single Pot Still
1.3.3.1.definition: Irish whiskey from malted and unmalted barley, distilled in pot stills at one distillery.

1.3.3.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Irish Whiskey › Single Malt
1.3.3.2.definition: Malt whisky from 100% malted barley produced at a single distillery.

1.3.3.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Irish Whiskey › Single Grain
1.3.3.3.definition: Grain whisky from a single distillery.

1.3.3.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Irish Whiskey › Blended
1.3.3.4.definition: A blend of malt (or pot still) whisky with grain whisky.

1.3.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Japanese Whisky
1.3.4.definition: Japanese Whisky is a group of 3 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Single Malt, Blended, Grain.

1.3.4.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Japanese Whisky › Single Malt
1.3.4.1.definition: Malt whisky from 100% malted barley produced at a single distillery.

1.3.4.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Japanese Whisky › Blended
1.3.4.2.definition: A blend of malt (or pot still) whisky with grain whisky.

1.3.4.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Japanese Whisky › Grain
1.3.4.3.definition: Whisky made from grains other than, or in addition to, malted barley, usually in column stills.

1.3.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Whisk(e)y
1.3.5.definition: Other Whisk(e)y is a group of 4 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Canadian Whisky, Indian Single Malt, Taiwanese Single Malt….

1.3.5.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Whisk(e)y › Canadian Whisky
1.3.5.1.definition: Whisky made and aged in Canada for at least 3 years in small wood, often from blended grains.

1.3.5.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Whisk(e)y › Indian Single Malt
1.3.5.2.definition: Malt whisky made in India, where warm climates speed up maturation.

1.3.5.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Whisk(e)y › Taiwanese Single Malt
1.3.5.3.definition: Malt whisky made in Taiwan, matured quickly in a subtropical climate.

1.3.5.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Whisk(e)y › Welsh Whisky

1.3.6.definition: Gin is a group of 7 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes London Dry, Plymouth, Old Tom….

1.3.6.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Gin › London Dry
1.3.6.1.definition: Gin style with all flavor from redistillation with botanicals and no added flavoring after distillation (sugar strictly limited).

1.3.6.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Gin › Plymouth
1.3.6.2.definition: Gin made in Plymouth, England; it formerly had its own geographical indication.

1.3.6.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Gin › Old Tom

1.3.6.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Gin › Genever (Jenever)
1.3.6.4.definition: Dutch and Belgian juniper spirit based on malt wine, the forerunner of gin.

1.3.6.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Gin › Navy Strength
1.3.6.5.definition: Gin or rum bottled at about 57% ABV (100 UK proof).

1.3.6.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Gin › Contemporary/New Western
1.3.6.6.definition: Gin styles where juniper is less dominant and other botanicals lead.

1.3.6.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Gin › Sloe Gin (liqueur)
1.3.6.7.definition: Gin-based liqueur flavored with sloe berries.

1.3.7.definition: Rum is a group of 9 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Light/White, Gold, Dark….

1.3.7.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Light/White
1.3.7.1.definition: Unaged or lightly aged, often filtered, clear rum.

1.3.7.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Gold
1.3.7.2.definition: Lightly aged or colored rum, between white and dark.

1.3.7.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Dark
1.3.7.3.definition: Rum with deep color from longer aging, added caramel or molasses.

1.3.7.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Overproof
1.3.7.4.definition: Spirit bottled well above standard strength.

1.3.7.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Spiced
1.3.7.5.definition: Rum flavored with spices such as vanilla and cinnamon.

1.3.7.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Rhum Agricole (AOC Martinique)
1.3.7.6.definition: Rum distilled from fresh sugarcane juice rather than molasses.

1.3.7.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Cachaça
1.3.7.7.definition: Brazilian spirit distilled from fermented fresh sugarcane juice.

1.3.7.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Jamaican pot-still
1.3.7.8.definition: Jamaican rum made in pot stills, often very high in esters.

1.3.7.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Rum › Demerara (Guyana)
1.3.7.9.definition: Rum from Guyana, notably made on historic wooden stills.

1.3.8.definition: Agave is a group of 11 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Tequila Blanco, Tequila Joven, Tequila Reposado….

1.3.8.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Tequila Blanco
1.3.8.1.definition: Unaged (or rested under 2 months) tequila; see Tequila aging rules (NOM-006).

1.3.8.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Tequila Joven
1.3.8.2.definition: Blend of blanco tequila with aged tequila, or blanco mellowed with permitted additives (abocado).

1.3.8.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Tequila Reposado
1.3.8.3.definition: Tequila matured at least 2 months in oak or encino (NOM-006).

1.3.8.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Tequila Añejo
1.3.8.4.definition: Tequila matured at least 1 year in oak or encino containers of up to 600 L (NOM-006).

1.3.8.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Tequila Extra Añejo
1.3.8.5.definition: Tequila matured at least 3 years in oak or encino containers of up to 600 L (NOM-006).

1.3.8.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Mezcal (Joven/Reposado/Añejo)
1.3.8.6.definition: Mexican agave spirit regulated by NOM-070, with classes by aging.

1.3.8.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Mezcal Ancestral
1.3.8.7.definition: Most traditional NOM-070 mezcal category: pit ovens, hand or tahona milling, clay-pot distillation.

1.3.8.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Mezcal Artesanal
1.3.8.8.definition: NOM-070 mezcal category with traditional cooking and milling, allowing copper stills.

1.3.8.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Raicilla
1.3.8.9.definition: Agave spirit from Jalisco, Mexico, with its own denomination of origin.

1.3.8.10.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Sotol (Dasylirion)
1.3.8.10.definition: Spirit from the desert spoon plant (Dasylirion) of northern Mexico.

1.3.8.11.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Agave › Bacanora
1.3.8.11.definition: Agave spirit from Sonora, Mexico, with its own denomination of origin.

1.3.9.definition: Brandy is a group of 10 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Cognac VS, Cognac VSOP, Cognac XO….

1.3.9.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Cognac VS
1.3.9.1.definition: Cognac whose youngest eau-de-vie is at least 2 years old.

1.3.9.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Cognac VSOP
1.3.9.2.definition: Cognac whose youngest eau-de-vie is at least 4 years old.

1.3.9.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Cognac XO
1.3.9.3.definition: Cognac whose youngest eau-de-vie is at least 10 years old.

1.3.9.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Armagnac
1.3.9.4.definition: Grape brandy from Gascony, traditionally single-distilled in a column still (alambic armagnacais).

1.3.9.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Brandy de Jerez
1.3.9.5.definition: Spanish brandy aged in Sherry casks using the solera system in the Jerez area.

1.3.9.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Pisco (Peru/Chile)
1.3.9.6.definition: Grape brandy from Peru or Chile, each with its own rules.

1.3.9.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Calvados
1.3.9.7.definition: Apple (and pear) brandy from Normandy under AOC rules.

1.3.9.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Grappa
1.3.9.8.definition: Italian spirit distilled from grape pomace.

1.3.9.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › Eau-de-vie (Kirsch/Poire Williams)
1.3.9.9.definition: Clear fruit brandy, e.g. Kirsch (cherry) or Poire Williams (pear).

1.3.9.10.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Brandy › American brandy
1.3.9.10.definition: Brandy made in the US, mostly from grapes and largely in California.

1.3.10.definition: Vodka is a group of 4 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Grain vodka, Potato vodka, Grape vodka….

1.3.10.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Vodka › Grain vodka
1.3.10.1.definition: Vodka distilled from cereals such as wheat or rye.

1.3.10.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Vodka › Potato vodka

1.3.10.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Vodka › Grape vodka

1.3.10.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Vodka › Flavored vodka
1.3.10.4.definition: Vodka with added natural or artificial flavors.

1.3.11.definition: Liqueurs is a group of 8 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Amaro, Orange liqueur (Triple sec/Curaçao), Herbal (Chartreuse/Bénédictine)….

1.3.11.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Liqueurs › Amaro

1.3.11.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Liqueurs › Orange liqueur (Triple sec/Curaçao)

1.3.11.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Liqueurs › Herbal (Chartreuse/Bénédictine)
1.3.11.3.definition: Liqueurs flavored with many herbs, historically made by monks.

1.3.11.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Liqueurs › Anise (Pastis/Ouzo/Sambuca/Absinthe)
1.3.11.4.definition: Spirits and liqueurs flavored with anise or star anise; absinthe also contains wormwood.

1.3.11.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Liqueurs › Coffee liqueur
1.3.11.5.definition: Sweet liqueur flavored with coffee, e.g. Kahlúa.

1.3.11.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Liqueurs › Cream liqueur
1.3.11.6.definition: Liqueur blended with dairy cream, e.g. Irish cream.

1.3.11.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Liqueurs › Nut liqueur (Amaretto/Frangelico)
1.3.11.7.definition: Liqueurs flavored with nuts or apricot kernels.

1.3.11.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Liqueurs › Fruit liqueur (Limoncello/Crème de cassis)
1.3.11.8.definition: Sweetened spirit flavored with fruit, e.g. lemon zest or blackcurrant.

1.3.12.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits
1.3.12.definition: Asian Spirits is a group of 8 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Baijiu: Strong aroma (nongxiang), Baijiu: Light aroma (qingxiang), Baijiu: Sauce aroma (jiangxiang)….

1.3.12.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits › Baijiu: Strong aroma (nongxiang)
1.3.12.1.definition: The most widely produced baijiu style, with fruity, pungent character; e.g. Wuliangye.

1.3.12.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits › Baijiu: Light aroma (qingxiang)
1.3.12.2.definition: Baijiu style with a clean, delicate profile, typified by Fenjiu.

1.3.12.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits › Baijiu: Sauce aroma (jiangxiang)
1.3.12.3.definition: Baijiu style with savory, soy-like character, typified by Moutai.

1.3.12.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits › Baijiu: Rice aroma (mixiang)
1.3.12.4.definition: Baijiu style made mainly from rice, with a soft profile, e.g. Guilin Sanhua.

1.3.12.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits › Shochu (honkaku)
1.3.12.5.definition: Japanese single-distilled spirit from ingredients such as barley, sweet potato or rice.

1.3.12.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits › Awamori
1.3.12.6.definition: Okinawan distilled spirit made from long-grain rice with black koji (Aspergillus luchuensis).

1.3.12.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits › Soju
1.3.12.7.definition: Korean distilled spirit, traditionally from rice; mass-market versions are diluted and sweetened.

1.3.12.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Asian Spirits › Arrack
1.3.12.8.definition: South and Southeast Asian spirits made from palm sap, sugarcane or rice; for example Batavia arrack and Sri Lankan coconut arrack.

1.3.13.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Char Levels
1.3.13.definition: Char Levels is a group of 6 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes #1 char (light), #2 char, #3 char (common for bourbon)….

1.3.13.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Char Levels › #1 char (light)
1.3.13.1.definition: Lightest standard barrel char level, burned for about 15 seconds by common cooperage convention.

1.3.13.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Char Levels › #2 char

1.3.13.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Char Levels › #3 char (common for bourbon)
1.3.13.3.definition: Medium-heavy barrel char level, widely used for bourbon.

1.3.13.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Char Levels › #4 char (alligator)
1.3.13.4.definition: Heaviest standard char (about 55 seconds); the charred surface cracks into scales like alligator skin.

1.3.13.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Char Levels › Toast + char (two-step)
1.3.13.5.definition: Barrel heat treatment that toasts the wood first and then chars it.

1.3.13.6.term: See Wine Academy: oak, forests, sizes
1.3.13.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Char Levels › See Wine Academy: oak, forests, sizes
1.3.13.6.definition: Cross-reference: oak species, forests and barrel sizes are covered in the Wine Academy.

1.3.14.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes
1.3.14.definition: Cask Finishes is a group of 11 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes Ex-bourbon, Oloroso sherry, Pedro Ximénez (PX) sherry….

1.3.14.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Ex-bourbon
1.3.14.1.definition: Used bourbon barrels, the most common cask for maturing Scotch.

1.3.14.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Oloroso sherry
1.3.14.2.definition: Casks seasoned with oxidatively aged Oloroso Sherry, used for maturation or finishing.

1.3.14.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Pedro Ximénez (PX) sherry
1.3.14.3.definition: Casks seasoned with sweet PX Sherry, used for finishing.

1.3.14.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Fino/Amontillado sherry
1.3.14.4.definition: Casks seasoned with dry Sherry, used to finish spirits.

1.3.14.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Port (ruby/tawny)
1.3.14.5.definition: Casks that previously held Port wine, used to finish spirits.

1.3.14.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Madeira
1.3.14.6.definition: Casks that previously held Madeira wine, used to finish spirits.

1.3.14.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Sauternes
1.3.14.7.definition: Sweet white Bordeaux wine from Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc affected by noble rot.

1.3.14.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Red wine
1.3.14.8.definition: Casks that previously held red wine, used to finish spirits.

1.3.14.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Rum cask
1.3.14.9.definition: Casks that previously held rum, used to finish other spirits.

1.3.14.10.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Cognac cask
1.3.14.10.definition: Casks that previously held Cognac, used to finish other spirits.

1.3.14.11.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Cask Finishes › Beer/stout cask
1.3.14.11.definition: Casks that previously held beer, used to finish whisky.

1.3.15.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Maturation Systems
1.3.15.definition: Maturation Systems is a group of 7 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes Solera (criaderas y solera), Angel's share (evaporation), Dunnage warehouse….

1.3.15.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Maturation Systems › Solera (criaderas y solera)
1.3.15.1.definition: Fractional blending system where younger wine tops up older barrels, so each bottling is a blend of ages.

1.3.15.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Maturation Systems › Angel's share (evaporation)
1.3.15.2.definition: Spirit lost to evaporation through the cask during aging.

1.3.15.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Maturation Systems › Dunnage warehouse
1.3.15.3.definition: Traditional low, earth-floored warehouse with casks stacked a few high.

1.3.15.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Maturation Systems › Rickhouse (rackhouse)
1.3.15.4.definition: Multi-story warehouse with barrels on wooden racks, typical for bourbon.

1.3.15.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Maturation Systems › Palletized warehouse
1.3.15.5.definition: Warehouse where casks are stored upright on pallets.

1.3.15.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Maturation Systems › Tropical maturation
1.3.15.6.definition: Aging in hot climates, where faster evaporation and wood interaction speed up maturation.

1.3.15.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Maturation Systems › Bottled-in-Bond (≥4 years, US)
1.3.15.7.definition: US designation: one distiller, one season, aged at least 4 years in a bonded warehouse, bottled at 100 proof.

1.3.16.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Agave Aging (NOM-006)
1.3.16.definition: Agave Aging (NOM-006) is a group of 4 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes Tequila Reposado (≥2 months in oak), Tequila Añejo (≥1 year, ≤600 L oak), Tequila Extra Añejo (≥3 years, ≤600 L oak)….

1.3.16.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Agave Aging (NOM-006) › Tequila Reposado (≥2 months in oak)
1.3.16.1.definition: Tequila matured at least 2 months in oak or encino (NOM-006).

1.3.16.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Agave Aging (NOM-006) › Tequila Añejo (≥1 year, ≤600 L oak)
1.3.16.2.definition: Tequila matured at least 1 year in oak or encino containers of up to 600 L (NOM-006).

1.3.16.3.term: Tequila Extra Añejo (≥3 years, ≤600 L oak)
1.3.16.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Agave Aging (NOM-006) › Tequila Extra Añejo (≥3 years, ≤600 L oak)
1.3.16.3.definition: Tequila matured at least 3 years in oak or encino containers of up to 600 L (NOM-006).

1.3.16.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Agave Aging (NOM-006) › Cristalino (aged, then filtered)
1.3.16.4.definition: Aged tequila that has been filtered (often through charcoal) to remove color; an industry term, not a NOM class.

1.3.17.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Regional Spirits
1.3.17.definition: Other Regional Spirits is a group of 7 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Aquavit (akvavit), Rakı, Arak….

1.3.17.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Regional Spirits › Aquavit (akvavit)
1.3.17.1.definition: Scandinavian spirit flavored mainly with caraway or dill.

1.3.17.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Regional Spirits › Rakı

1.3.17.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Regional Spirits › Arak
1.3.17.3.definition: Anise-flavored grape spirit of the Levant.

1.3.17.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Regional Spirits › Pálinka
1.3.17.4.definition: Hungarian fruit brandy with protected status.

1.3.17.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Regional Spirits › Slivovitz (šljivovica)
1.3.17.5.definition: Plum brandy of Central and Eastern Europe.

1.3.17.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Regional Spirits › Singani
1.3.17.6.definition: Bolivian grape brandy made from Muscat of Alexandria.

1.3.17.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Other Regional Spirits › Feni
1.3.17.7.definition: Goan spirit made from cashew apple or coconut palm sap.

1.3.18.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables
1.3.18.definition: The Unforgettables is a group of 10 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Cocktails (IBA). It includes Old Fashioned, Manhattan, Dry Martini….

1.3.18.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Old Fashioned
1.3.18.1.definition: Cocktail of whiskey, sugar, bitters and a twist of citrus peel.

1.3.18.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Manhattan
1.3.18.2.definition: Cocktail of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters.

1.3.18.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Dry Martini
1.3.18.3.definition: Cocktail of gin (or vodka) and dry vermouth.

1.3.18.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Negroni
1.3.18.4.definition: Cocktail of equal parts gin, sweet vermouth and Campari.

1.3.18.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Daiquiri
1.3.18.5.definition: Cocktail of rum, lime juice and sugar.

1.3.18.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Whiskey Sour
1.3.18.6.definition: Cocktail of whiskey, lemon, sugar and optionally egg white.

1.3.18.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Sidecar
1.3.18.7.definition: Cocktail of Cognac, orange liqueur and lemon.

1.3.18.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Sazerac
1.3.18.8.definition: New Orleans cocktail of rye or Cognac, sugar, Peychaud's bitters and an absinthe rinse.

1.3.18.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Boulevardier
1.3.18.9.definition: Cocktail of bourbon or rye, sweet vermouth and Campari.

1.3.18.10.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › The Unforgettables › Martinez
1.3.18.10.definition: Cocktail of gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino and bitters, a predecessor of the Martini.

1.3.19.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics
1.3.19.definition: Contemporary Classics is a group of 10 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Cocktails (IBA). It includes Margarita, Mojito, Cosmopolitan….

1.3.19.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Margarita
1.3.19.1.definition: Cocktail of tequila, orange liqueur and lime juice.

1.3.19.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Mojito
1.3.19.2.definition: Cuban cocktail of white rum, lime, sugar, mint and soda water.

1.3.19.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Cosmopolitan
1.3.19.3.definition: Cocktail of vodka, orange liqueur, cranberry juice and lime.

1.3.19.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Moscow Mule
1.3.19.4.definition: Cocktail of vodka, ginger beer and lime.

1.3.19.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Mai Tai
1.3.19.5.definition: Tiki cocktail of rum, lime, orange curaçao and orgeat.

1.3.19.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Piña Colada
1.3.19.6.definition: Cocktail of rum, pineapple and coconut cream.

1.3.19.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Bloody Mary
1.3.19.7.definition: Cocktail of vodka, tomato juice and savory seasonings.

1.3.19.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Caipirinha
1.3.19.8.definition: Brazilian cocktail of cachaça, lime and sugar.

1.3.19.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › Mimosa
1.3.19.9.definition: Drink of sparkling wine and orange juice.

1.3.19.10.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › Contemporary Classics › French 75
1.3.19.10.definition: Cocktail of gin, lemon, sugar and Champagne.

1.3.20.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › New Era Drinks
1.3.20.definition: New Era Drinks is a group of 6 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Cocktails (IBA). It includes Espresso Martini, Spritz Veneziano, Penicillin….

1.3.20.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › New Era Drinks › Espresso Martini
1.3.20.1.definition: Cocktail of vodka, espresso and coffee liqueur.

1.3.20.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › New Era Drinks › Spritz Veneziano
1.3.20.2.definition: Venetian drink of Prosecco, a bitter aperitif and soda water.

1.3.20.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › New Era Drinks › Penicillin
1.3.20.3.definition: Modern cocktail of blended Scotch, lemon, honey-ginger syrup and a float of peated Scotch.

1.3.20.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › New Era Drinks › Paper Plane
1.3.20.4.definition: Modern cocktail of bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino and lemon in equal parts.

1.3.20.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › New Era Drinks › Tommy's Margarita
1.3.20.5.definition: Margarita variation with agave syrup instead of orange liqueur.

1.3.20.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cocktails (IBA) › New Era Drinks › Naked and Famous
1.3.20.6.definition: Modern cocktail of mezcal, Yellow Chartreuse, Aperol and lime in equal parts.

1.3.21.definition: Zero-Proof is a group of 5 entries in the Spirits Academy. It includes Virgin cocktails (mocktails), Non-alcoholic gin alternatives, Non-alcoholic whiskey alternatives….

1.3.21.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Zero-Proof › Virgin cocktails (mocktails)

1.3.21.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Zero-Proof › Non-alcoholic gin alternatives
1.3.21.2.definition: Alcohol-free botanical distillates or infusions in a gin style.

1.3.21.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Zero-Proof › Non-alcoholic whiskey alternatives

1.3.21.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Zero-Proof › Non-alcoholic aperitif/bitter alternatives
1.3.21.4.definition: Alcohol-free drinks that imitate bitter aperitifs.

1.3.21.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Zero-Proof › Shrub-based drinks
1.3.21.5.definition: Drinks made with shrub, a vinegar-based fruit syrup.

1.3.22.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials
1.3.22.definition: Raw Materials is a group of 12 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Corn, Rye, Malted barley….

1.3.22.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Corn
1.3.22.1.definition: Main grain of bourbon (at least 51% of the mash) and the base of corn whiskey.

1.3.22.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Rye
1.3.22.2.definition: Spicy grain used in rye whiskey and bourbon mash bills.

1.3.22.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Malted barley
1.3.22.3.definition: Barley that has been germinated and dried; the base of malt whisky.

1.3.22.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Wheat
1.3.22.4.definition: Grain used in wheated bourbon, wheat whiskey and many vodkas.

1.3.22.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Sugarcane juice
1.3.22.5.definition: Fresh cane juice, the base of rhum agricole and cachaça.

1.3.22.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Molasses
1.3.22.6.definition: Sugar-refining by-product and the base of most rum.

1.3.22.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Grapes/wine
1.3.22.7.definition: Raw material for brandies such as Cognac, Armagnac and pisco.

1.3.22.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Apples & pears
1.3.22.8.definition: Fruit raw materials for cider brandies such as Calvados and for pear eaux-de-vie.

1.3.22.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Blue agave (A. tequilana Weber)
1.3.22.9.definition: Agave tequilana Weber var. azul, the only agave permitted for tequila.

1.3.22.10.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Potatoes
1.3.22.10.definition: Raw material for some vodkas and aquavits.

1.3.22.11.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Sorghum

1.3.22.12.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Raw Materials › Rice
1.3.22.12.definition: Raw material for shochu, awamori and some baijiu.

1.3.23.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Mash Bills
1.3.23.definition: Mash Bills is a group of 6 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Bourbon (≥51% corn), Rye whiskey (≥51% rye), High-rye bourbon….

1.3.23.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Mash Bills › Bourbon (≥51% corn)
1.3.23.1.definition: US whiskey made from at least 51% corn and aged in new charred oak containers.

1.3.23.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Mash Bills › Rye whiskey (≥51% rye)
1.3.23.2.definition: US whiskey made from at least 51% rye and aged in new charred oak.

1.3.23.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Mash Bills › High-rye bourbon
1.3.23.3.definition: Bourbon with a relatively high share of rye in its mash bill, giving spicier flavor.

1.3.23.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Mash Bills › Wheated bourbon
1.3.23.4.definition: Bourbon that uses wheat instead of rye as its secondary grain.

1.3.23.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Mash Bills › Single malt (100% malted barley)
1.3.23.5.definition: Whisky made from 100% malted barley at one distillery.

1.3.23.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Mash Bills › Four-grain
1.3.23.6.definition: Mash bill using corn, rye, wheat and malted barley.

1.3.24.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Fermentation
1.3.24.definition: Fermentation is a group of 6 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Production. It includes Sweet mash, Sour mash (backset), Wash (distiller's beer)….

1.3.24.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Fermentation › Sweet mash
1.3.24.1.definition: Mash started fresh, without backset from a previous distillation.

1.3.24.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Fermentation › Sour mash (backset)
1.3.24.2.definition: Adding spent mash from a previous distillation to a new mash for acidity and consistency.

1.3.24.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Fermentation › Wash (distiller's beer)
1.3.24.3.definition: Fermented liquid that goes into the still.

1.3.24.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Fermentation › Open vs closed fermenters
1.3.24.4.definition: Fermenting in open vats, exposed to air and wild microbes, versus closed tanks.

1.3.24.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Fermentation › Dunder (Jamaican rum)
1.3.24.5.definition: Leftover liquid from previous distillations, used in Jamaican rum production to build heavy flavor.

1.3.24.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Fermentation › Solid-state fermentation (baijiu)
1.3.24.6.definition: Fermenting moist grain with qu starter in pits or piles rather than in liquid; characteristic of baijiu.

1.3.25.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation
1.3.25.definition: Distillation is a group of 12 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Production. It includes Pot still, Column (Coffey) still, Hybrid still….

1.3.25.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Pot still
1.3.25.1.definition: Batch still, usually copper, used for malt whisky, Cognac and many rums.

1.3.25.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Column (Coffey) still
1.3.25.2.definition: Continuous still that can produce high-strength, lighter spirit efficiently.

1.3.25.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Hybrid still
1.3.25.3.definition: Pot still with an attached rectifying column, able to make different spirit styles.

1.3.25.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Alembic charentais
1.3.25.4.definition: Traditional copper pot still used for Cognac's double distillation.

1.3.25.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Double distillation
1.3.25.5.definition: Distilling twice in pot stills, as for most Scotch malt whisky and Cognac.

1.3.25.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Triple distillation
1.3.25.6.definition: Distilling three times, traditional in much Irish whiskey and in some Lowland Scotch.

1.3.25.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Doubler/thumper
1.3.25.7.definition: Secondary pot vessel in American distilling that redistills the spirit vapor from the first still.

1.3.25.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Heads (foreshots)
1.3.25.8.definition: First, most volatile part of a distillation run, usually discarded or recycled.

1.3.25.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Hearts
1.3.25.9.definition: Middle part of a distillation run kept as the spirit.

1.3.25.10.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Tails (feints)
1.3.25.10.definition: Final part of a distillation run, heavier and oilier, usually recycled.

1.3.25.11.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Reflux
1.3.25.11.definition: Vapor that condenses and falls back in a still; more reflux gives a lighter, purer spirit.

1.3.25.12.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Distillation › Proof & ABV
1.3.25.12.definition: US proof is twice the ABV (100 proof = 50% ABV).

1.3.26.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production
1.3.26.definition: Agave Production is a group of 9 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Production. It includes Jimador harvest (coa), Piñas, Earthen pit oven (mezcal)….

1.3.26.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Jimador harvest (coa)
1.3.26.1.definition: Agave harvest by jimadores, who cut leaves off the agave heart with a sharp tool called a coa.

1.3.26.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Piñas
1.3.26.2.definition: Harvested agave hearts, cooked to convert their inulin into fermentable sugars.

1.3.26.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Earthen pit oven (mezcal)
1.3.26.3.definition: Underground pit lined with stones and fired with wood, used to roast agave; it gives mezcal its smoky character.

1.3.26.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Masonry horno
1.3.26.4.definition: Above-ground masonry oven used to steam-cook agave for tequila.

1.3.26.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Autoclave
1.3.26.5.definition: Pressurized steam oven used by some tequila producers to cook agave quickly.

1.3.26.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Diffuser (difusor)
1.3.26.6.definition: Machine that extracts sugars from raw agave with water and pressure, sometimes with acid.

1.3.26.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Tahona (stone wheel)
1.3.26.7.definition: Large stone wheel used to crush cooked agave.

1.3.26.8.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Roller mill
1.3.26.8.definition: Mill that crushes malt or grain between rollers.

1.3.26.9.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Production › Agave Production › Copper & clay pot stills
1.3.26.9.definition: Small stills used for traditional mezcal; clay pots are required for the Ancestral category.

1.3.27.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Techniques › Finishing & Bottling
1.3.27.definition: Finishing & Bottling is a group of 7 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Techniques. It includes Proofing (dilution), Chill filtration, Non-chill filtered….

1.3.27.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Techniques › Finishing & Bottling › Proofing (dilution)
1.3.27.1.definition: Adding water to bring spirit down to bottling strength.

1.3.27.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Techniques › Finishing & Bottling › Chill filtration
1.3.27.2.definition: Chilling and filtering whisky to remove compounds that can cause cloudiness when cold.

1.3.27.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Techniques › Finishing & Bottling › Non-chill filtered
1.3.27.3.definition: Whisky bottled without chill filtration, keeping more texture.

1.3.27.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Techniques › Finishing & Bottling › Cask strength
1.3.27.4.definition: Spirit bottled at or near the strength it came out of the cask, without dilution.

1.3.27.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Techniques › Finishing & Bottling › Blending (vatting)
1.3.27.5.definition: Combining whiskies or spirits from different casks or batches for a consistent style. 'Vatting' traditionally means mixing malts.

1.3.27.6.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Techniques › Finishing & Bottling › Caramel color (E150a)
1.3.27.6.definition: Plain caramel coloring, permitted in Scotch whisky and many spirits to adjust color.

1.3.27.7.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Techniques › Finishing & Bottling › See Barrel Toasting & Aging
1.3.27.7.definition: Cross-reference: see this academy's Barrel Toasting & Aging section.

1.3.28.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Tequila (NOM-006)
1.3.28.definition: Tequila (NOM-006) is a group of 5 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Aging Requirements. It includes Blanco/Plata · no aging (may rest <2 mo), Joven/Oro · blend or abocado, Reposado · 2+ mo oak….
facts: Blanco/Plata: no abocante, may mature <2 months in oak/encino (§4.36.1). Joven/Oro: blanco blended with reposado/añejo/extra añejo, or blanco mellowed with permitted abocado ingredients (§4.36.2). Aged classes: oak or holm-oak (encino), direct contact. Reposado has NO vessel-size limit and no legal upper bound (the popular '2–12 months' reflects that ≥1 yr in ≤600 L qualifies as Añejo). Source: NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36 (DOF 13-12-2012) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.28.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Tequila (NOM-006) › Blanco/Plata · no aging (may rest <2 mo)
1.3.28.1.definition: Tequila class bottled without abocado (mellowing additives); it may rest under 2 months in oak or encino (NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36.1). Requirement: no aging (may rest <2 mo).
facts: Blanco/Plata: no abocante, may mature <2 months in oak/encino (§4.36.1). Joven/Oro: blanco blended with reposado/añejo/extra añejo, or blanco mellowed with permitted abocado ingredients (§4.36.2). Aged classes: oak or holm-oak (encino), direct contact. Reposado has NO vessel-size limit and no legal upper bound (the popular '2–12 months' reflects that ≥1 yr in ≤600 L qualifies as Añejo). Source: NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36 (DOF 13-12-2012) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.28.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Tequila (NOM-006) › Joven/Oro · blend or abocado
1.3.28.2.definition: Tequila class made by blending blanco with reposado, añejo or extra añejo tequila, or by mellowing blanco with permitted additives (abocado) (NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36.2). Requirement: blend or abocado.
facts: Blanco/Plata: no abocante, may mature <2 months in oak/encino (§4.36.1). Joven/Oro: blanco blended with reposado/añejo/extra añejo, or blanco mellowed with permitted abocado ingredients (§4.36.2). Aged classes: oak or holm-oak (encino), direct contact. Reposado has NO vessel-size limit and no legal upper bound (the popular '2–12 months' reflects that ≥1 yr in ≤600 L qualifies as Añejo). Source: NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36 (DOF 13-12-2012) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.28.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Tequila (NOM-006) › Reposado · 2+ mo oak
1.3.28.3.definition: Tequila matured at least 2 months in direct contact with oak or encino wood, with no vessel-size limit (NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36.3). Requirement: 2+ mo oak.
facts: Blanco/Plata: no abocante, may mature <2 months in oak/encino (§4.36.1). Joven/Oro: blanco blended with reposado/añejo/extra añejo, or blanco mellowed with permitted abocado ingredients (§4.36.2). Aged classes: oak or holm-oak (encino), direct contact. Reposado has NO vessel-size limit and no legal upper bound (the popular '2–12 months' reflects that ≥1 yr in ≤600 L qualifies as Añejo). Source: NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36 (DOF 13-12-2012) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.28.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Tequila (NOM-006) › Añejo · 1+ yr oak ≤600 L
1.3.28.4.definition: Tequila matured at least 1 year in oak or encino containers of up to 600 L (NOM-006-SCFI-2012). Requirement: 1+ yr oak ≤600 L.
facts: Blanco/Plata: no abocante, may mature <2 months in oak/encino (§4.36.1). Joven/Oro: blanco blended with reposado/añejo/extra añejo, or blanco mellowed with permitted abocado ingredients (§4.36.2). Aged classes: oak or holm-oak (encino), direct contact. Reposado has NO vessel-size limit and no legal upper bound (the popular '2–12 months' reflects that ≥1 yr in ≤600 L qualifies as Añejo). Source: NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36 (DOF 13-12-2012) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.28.5.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Tequila (NOM-006) › Extra Añejo · 3+ yr oak ≤600 L
1.3.28.5.definition: Tequila matured at least 3 years in oak or encino containers of up to 600 L (NOM-006-SCFI-2012). Requirement: 3+ yr oak ≤600 L.
facts: Blanco/Plata: no abocante, may mature <2 months in oak/encino (§4.36.1). Joven/Oro: blanco blended with reposado/añejo/extra añejo, or blanco mellowed with permitted abocado ingredients (§4.36.2). Aged classes: oak or holm-oak (encino), direct contact. Reposado has NO vessel-size limit and no legal upper bound (the popular '2–12 months' reflects that ≥1 yr in ≤600 L qualifies as Añejo). Source: NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36 (DOF 13-12-2012) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.29.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Mezcal (NOM-070)
1.3.29.definition: Mezcal (NOM-070) is a group of 4 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Aging Requirements. It includes Blanco/Joven · no aging, Madurado en vidrio · 12+ mo glass, Reposado · 2–12 mo wood….
facts: NOM-070 §4.5: Blanco o Joven = colorless, translucent, no subsequent process; Madurado en Vidrio = stabilized in glass >12 months underground or in a space with minimal light/temperature/humidity variation; Reposado = 2–12 months in wood, no restriction on vessel size/shape; Añejo = >12 months in wood vessels <1,000 L. Madurado en Vidrio and Añejo labels must state age in whole years. Source: NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5 (DOF 23-02-2017, dof.gob.mx) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.29.1.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Mezcal (NOM-070) › Blanco/Joven · no aging
1.3.29.1.definition: Mezcal class that is colorless and translucent and receives no further process after distillation (NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5). Requirement: no aging.
facts: NOM-070 §4.5: Blanco o Joven = colorless, translucent, no subsequent process; Madurado en Vidrio = stabilized in glass >12 months underground or in a space with minimal light/temperature/humidity variation; Reposado = 2–12 months in wood, no restriction on vessel size/shape; Añejo = >12 months in wood vessels <1,000 L. Madurado en Vidrio and Añejo labels must state age in whole years. Source: NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5 (DOF 23-02-2017, dof.gob.mx) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.29.2.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Mezcal (NOM-070) › Madurado en vidrio · 12+ mo glass
1.3.29.2.definition: Mezcal class stabilized in glass for more than 12 months, underground or in a space with minimal light, temperature and humidity variation (NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5). Requirement: 12+ mo glass.
facts: NOM-070 §4.5: Blanco o Joven = colorless, translucent, no subsequent process; Madurado en Vidrio = stabilized in glass >12 months underground or in a space with minimal light/temperature/humidity variation; Reposado = 2–12 months in wood, no restriction on vessel size/shape; Añejo = >12 months in wood vessels <1,000 L. Madurado en Vidrio and Añejo labels must state age in whole years. Source: NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5 (DOF 23-02-2017, dof.gob.mx) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.29.3.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Mezcal (NOM-070) › Reposado · 2–12 mo wood
1.3.29.3.definition: Mezcal class rested 2–12 months in wooden vessels of any size or shape (NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5). Requirement: 2–12 mo wood.
facts: NOM-070 §4.5: Blanco o Joven = colorless, translucent, no subsequent process; Madurado en Vidrio = stabilized in glass >12 months underground or in a space with minimal light/temperature/humidity variation; Reposado = 2–12 months in wood, no restriction on vessel size/shape; Añejo = >12 months in wood vessels <1,000 L. Madurado en Vidrio and Añejo labels must state age in whole years. Source: NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5 (DOF 23-02-2017, dof.gob.mx) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.29.4.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Mezcal (NOM-070) › Añejo · 12+ mo wood <1,000 L
1.3.29.4.definition: Mezcal class aged more than 12 months in wooden vessels under 1,000 L; the label must state its age in whole years (NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5). Requirement: 12+ mo wood <1,000 L.
facts: NOM-070 §4.5: Blanco o Joven = colorless, translucent, no subsequent process; Madurado en Vidrio = stabilized in glass >12 months underground or in a space with minimal light/temperature/humidity variation; Reposado = 2–12 months in wood, no restriction on vessel size/shape; Añejo = >12 months in wood vessels <1,000 L. Madurado en Vidrio and Añejo labels must state age in whole years. Source: NOM-070-SCFI-2016 §4.5 (DOF 23-02-2017, dof.gob.mx) [verified online 2026-10-12]

1.3.30.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Whisk(e)y
1.3.30.definition: Whisk(e)y is a group of 8 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Aging Requirements. It includes Scotch · 3 yr oak ≤700 L, Japanese (JSLMA) · 3 yr wood ≤700 L, Irish · 3 yr wood….

2.1.1.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Species › Excelsa
2.1.1.4.definition: Coffee now classified as a variety of Coffea liberica (var. dewevrei), with tart, fruity flavor.

2.1.2.definition: Processing is a group of 6 entries in the Coffee Academy. It includes Washed (wet), Natural (dry), Honey (pulped natural)….

2.1.2.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Processing › Washed (wet)
2.1.2.1.definition: Processing method where fruit is removed and beans are fermented and washed before drying, giving a clean cup.

2.1.2.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Processing › Natural (dry)
2.1.2.2.definition: Processing method where whole coffee cherries are dried with the fruit on.

2.1.2.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Processing › Honey (pulped natural)
2.1.2.3.definition: Processing method where skin is removed but some sticky mucilage is left on during drying.

2.1.2.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Processing › Wet-hulled (Giling Basah)
2.1.2.4.definition: Indonesian process that removes parchment while the beans are still moist.

2.1.2.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Processing › Anaerobic fermentation
2.1.2.5.definition: Processing in which coffee cherries or beans ferment in sealed, low-oxygen tanks, often giving intense, unusual flavors.

2.1.2.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Processing › Carbonic maceration
2.1.2.6.definition: Whole, uncrushed grapes ferment inside a CO2-filled vessel, giving fruity, low-tannin reds (as in Beaujolais).

2.1.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Roast Level
2.1.3.definition: Roast Level is a group of 4 entries in the Coffee Academy. It includes Light (cinnamon/New England), Medium (City/American), Medium-dark (Full City)….

2.1.3.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Roast Level › Light (cinnamon/New England)
2.1.3.1.definition: Light roast levels ending near first crack.

2.1.3.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Roast Level › Medium (City/American)
2.1.3.2.definition: Medium roast levels, typically ending shortly after first crack.

2.1.3.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Roast Level › Medium-dark (Full City)

2.1.3.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Roast Level › Dark (Vienna/French/Italian)
2.1.3.4.definition: Roast levels beyond second crack, with oily surfaces and roast-dominant flavor.

2.1.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks
2.1.4.definition: Espresso Drinks is a group of 11 entries in the Coffee Academy. It includes Espresso, Ristretto, Lungo….

2.1.4.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Espresso
2.1.4.1.definition: Concentrated coffee made by forcing hot water through finely ground coffee at about 9 bar.

2.1.4.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Ristretto

2.1.4.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Lungo
2.1.4.3.definition: A longer espresso pulled with more water.

2.1.4.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Americano

2.1.4.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Macchiato
2.1.4.5.definition: Espresso 'marked' with a small amount of milk foam.

2.1.4.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Cortado
2.1.4.6.definition: Espresso cut with a roughly equal amount of warm milk.

2.1.4.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Flat white
2.1.4.7.definition: Espresso drink with a thin layer of microfoamed milk, smaller than a latte.

2.1.4.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Cappuccino
2.1.4.8.definition: Espresso with steamed milk and a thick layer of milk foam.

2.1.4.9.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Latte
2.1.4.9.definition: Espresso with a larger amount of steamed milk and a thin foam layer.

2.1.4.10.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Mocha
2.1.4.10.definition: Espresso with chocolate and steamed milk. The name also refers to the historic Yemeni port of Mocha.

2.1.4.11.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Espresso Drinks › Affogato
2.1.4.11.definition: Espresso poured over a scoop of ice cream or gelato.

2.1.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods
2.1.5.definition: Brew Methods is a group of 10 entries in the Coffee Academy. It includes Pour-over (V60/Chemex/Kalita), French press, AeroPress….

2.1.5.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › Pour-over (V60/Chemex/Kalita)
2.1.5.1.definition: Manual filter brewing by pouring water over coffee in a dripper.

2.1.5.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › French press
2.1.5.2.definition: Immersion brewer with a metal mesh plunger.

2.1.5.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › AeroPress
2.1.5.3.definition: Hand-pressed immersion brewer, invented in 2005, that pushes coffee through a paper or metal filter.

2.1.5.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › Moka pot
2.1.5.4.definition: Stovetop brewer using steam pressure to push water up through coffee.

2.1.5.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › Siphon
2.1.5.5.definition: Vacuum brewer using vapor pressure and suction.

2.1.5.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › Drip (batch brew)
2.1.5.6.definition: Automatic machine brewing that drips hot water over ground coffee in a filter.

2.1.5.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › Turkish (cezve)
2.1.5.7.definition: Finely ground coffee simmered in a small pot (cezve) and served unfiltered.

2.1.5.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › Cold brew
2.1.5.8.definition: Coffee extracted with cold or room-temperature water over many hours.

2.1.5.9.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › Cold drip (Kyoto)
2.1.5.9.definition: Cold water dripped slowly through coffee over several hours.

2.1.5.10.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Brew Methods › Phin (Vietnamese)
2.1.5.10.definition: Small metal drip filter used for Vietnamese coffee.

2.1.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel-Aged Coffee
2.1.6.definition: Barrel-Aged Coffee is a group of 4 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Barrel Toasting & Aging. It includes Green beans rested in bourbon barrels, Rum barrel-aged beans, Wine barrel-aged beans….

2.1.6.1.term: Green beans rested in bourbon barrels
2.1.6.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel-Aged Coffee › Green beans rested in bourbon barrels
2.1.6.1.definition: Green coffee stored in used bourbon barrels before roasting so it absorbs barrel aromas.

2.1.6.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel-Aged Coffee › Rum barrel-aged beans
2.1.6.2.definition: Green coffee aged in used rum barrels before roasting.

2.1.6.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel-Aged Coffee › Wine barrel-aged beans
2.1.6.3.definition: Green coffee aged in used wine barrels before roasting.

2.1.6.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel-Aged Coffee › Whiskey barrel-aged cold brew
2.1.6.4.definition: Cold brew made from coffee aged in used whiskey barrels.

2.1.7.definition: Decaffeination is a group of 4 entries in the Coffee Academy. It includes Swiss Water Process, CO2 (supercritical) process, Ethyl acetate (sugarcane) process….

2.1.7.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Decaffeination › Swiss Water Process
2.1.7.1.definition: Chemical-free decaffeination using water and activated carbon to remove caffeine.

2.1.7.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Decaffeination › CO2 (supercritical) process
2.1.7.2.definition: Decaffeination using pressurized, supercritical carbon dioxide to dissolve caffeine.

2.1.7.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Decaffeination › Ethyl acetate (sugarcane) process
2.1.7.3.definition: Decaffeination with ethyl acetate solvent, often made from sugarcane and marketed as 'natural decaf'.

2.1.7.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Decaffeination › Methylene chloride (direct/indirect) process
2.1.7.4.definition: Decaffeination with dichloromethane solvent, either directly on beans or on water used to soak them.

2.1.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Coffee Formats
2.1.8.definition: Coffee Formats is a group of 7 entries in the Coffee Academy. It includes Whole bean, Ground, Instant (freeze-dried)….

2.1.8.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Coffee Formats › Whole bean

2.1.8.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Coffee Formats › Ground

2.1.8.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Coffee Formats › Instant (freeze-dried)
2.1.8.3.definition: Soluble coffee made by freezing coffee extract and removing the water under vacuum.

2.1.8.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Coffee Formats › Instant (spray-dried)
2.1.8.4.definition: Soluble coffee made by spraying coffee extract into hot air.

2.1.8.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Coffee Formats › Single-serve pods/capsules
2.1.8.5.definition: Pre-portioned coffee in capsules or pods for brewing machines.

2.1.8.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Coffee Formats › Coffee concentrate
2.1.8.6.definition: Strong coffee extract meant to be diluted before drinking.

2.1.8.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Coffee Formats › Drip bags
2.1.8.7.definition: Single-serve filter pouches of ground coffee that hang over a cup.

2.1.9.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks
2.1.9.definition: Iced & Blended Drinks is a group of 8 entries in the Coffee Academy. It includes Iced coffee, Iced latte, Nitro cold brew….

2.1.9.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks › Iced coffee

2.1.9.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks › Iced latte
2.1.9.2.definition: Espresso with cold milk over ice.

2.1.9.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks › Nitro cold brew
2.1.9.3.definition: Cold brew infused with nitrogen for a creamy texture.

2.1.9.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks › Frappé (Greek)
2.1.9.4.definition: Shaken iced instant coffee, popular in Greece.

2.1.9.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks › Blended iced coffee (frappuccino-style)
2.1.9.5.definition: Coffee blended with ice, milk and sweetener into a slush.

2.1.9.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks › Espresso tonic
2.1.9.6.definition: Espresso poured over tonic water and ice.

2.1.9.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks › Dalgona coffee
2.1.9.7.definition: Whipped instant coffee, sugar and water spooned over milk.

2.1.9.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Iced & Blended Drinks › Shakerato
2.1.9.8.definition: Espresso shaken with ice and sugar.

2.1.10.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties
2.1.10.definition: Arabica Varieties is a group of 12 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Typica, Bourbon, Caturra….

2.1.10.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Typica
2.1.10.1.definition: One of the original Arabica varieties spread from Yemen and Java.

2.1.10.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Bourbon
