2.1.10.2.definition: Arabica coffee variety descended from plants taken from Yemen to Bourbon island (now Réunion).

2.1.10.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Caturra
2.1.10.3.definition: Compact natural mutation of Bourbon, discovered in Brazil.

2.1.10.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Catuaí
2.1.10.4.definition: Compact Brazilian variety from a Mundo Novo × Caturra cross.

2.1.10.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Mundo Novo
2.1.10.5.definition: Brazilian natural cross between Bourbon and Sumatra (Typica).

2.1.10.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Geisha (Gesha)
2.1.10.6.definition: Arabica variety from Ethiopia, made famous by Panama, known for floral, tea-like flavor.

2.1.10.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › SL28
2.1.10.7.definition: Kenyan variety selected by Scott Laboratories in the 1930s, prized for cup quality.

2.1.10.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › SL34
2.1.10.8.definition: Kenyan variety selected by Scott Laboratories, prized for cup quality.

2.1.10.9.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Pacamara
2.1.10.9.definition: Large-bean Salvadoran cross of Pacas and Maragogype.

2.1.10.10.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Maragogype
2.1.10.10.definition: Large-bean Typica mutation discovered in Brazil.

2.1.10.11.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Villa Sarchi
2.1.10.11.definition: Compact Bourbon mutation from Costa Rica.

2.1.10.12.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Arabica Varieties › Pink Bourbon
2.1.10.12.definition: Pink-fruited Arabica from Huila, Colombia; its exact lineage is debated.

2.1.11.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars
2.1.11.definition: Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars is a group of 10 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Timor Hybrid, Catimor, Sarchimor….

2.1.11.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Timor Hybrid
2.1.11.1.definition: Natural Arabica × robusta hybrid found in Timor, the source of rust resistance in many varieties.

2.1.11.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Catimor
2.1.11.2.definition: Rust-resistant Arabica group from a Timor Hybrid × Caturra cross.

2.1.11.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Sarchimor
2.1.11.3.definition: Rust-resistant group from a Villa Sarchi × Timor Hybrid cross.

2.1.11.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Castillo
2.1.11.4.definition: Colombian rust-resistant variety released by Cenicafé in 2005, with Timor Hybrid ancestry.

2.1.11.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Colombia
2.1.11.5.definition: Major producer of washed Arabica, with harvests in most months across its regions.

2.1.11.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Ruiru 11
2.1.11.6.definition: Compact Kenyan hybrid variety resistant to coffee berry disease and leaf rust, released in 1985.

2.1.11.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Batian
2.1.11.7.definition: Kenyan disease-resistant Arabica variety released in 2010, with resistance to coffee leaf rust and coffee berry disease.

2.1.11.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Marsellesa

2.1.11.9.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Obatã

2.1.11.10.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Hybrids & Resistant Cultivars › Starmaya (F1 hybrid)
2.1.11.10.definition: F1 hybrid Arabica that can be propagated from seed.

2.1.12.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Ethiopian Landraces
2.1.12.definition: Ethiopian Landraces is a group of 5 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Ethiopian heirloom landraces, JARC 74110, JARC 74112….

2.1.12.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Ethiopian Landraces › Ethiopian heirloom landraces
2.1.12.1.definition: Thousands of genetically diverse local Arabica types grown in Ethiopia.

2.1.12.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Ethiopian Landraces › JARC 74110
2.1.12.2.definition: Ethiopian Arabica selection released by the Jimma Agricultural Research Center.

2.1.12.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Ethiopian Landraces › JARC 74112
2.1.12.3.definition: Ethiopian Arabica selection released by the Jimma Agricultural Research Center.

2.1.12.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Ethiopian Landraces › Kurume

2.1.12.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Ethiopian Landraces › Wolisho

2.1.13.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Robusta & Other Species
2.1.13.definition: Robusta & Other Species is a group of 4 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Robusta (C. canephora) clones, Conilon (Brazil), Liberica….

2.1.13.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Robusta & Other Species › Robusta (C. canephora) clones
2.1.13.1.definition: Coffea canephora, a hardier, higher-caffeine coffee species.

2.1.13.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Robusta & Other Species › Conilon (Brazil)
2.1.13.2.definition: Brazilian name for Coffea canephora grown mainly in Espírito Santo and Rondônia.

2.1.13.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Robusta & Other Species › Liberica
2.1.13.3.definition: Coffea liberica, a large-bean coffee species from West Africa.

2.1.13.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Robusta & Other Species › Excelsa (C. liberica var. dewevrei)
2.1.13.4.definition: Coffee now classified as a variety of Coffea liberica (var. dewevrei), with tart, fruity flavor.

2.1.14.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Conditions
2.1.14.definition: Growing Conditions is a group of 7 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Altitude (masl), Shade-grown, Full sun….

2.1.14.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Conditions › Altitude (masl)
2.1.14.1.definition: Farm elevation in meters above sea level. Higher altitudes generally slow cherry ripening and are associated with denser beans.

2.1.14.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Conditions › Shade-grown

2.1.14.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Conditions › Full sun
2.1.14.3.definition: Coffee grown without shade trees, usually giving higher yield at greater ecological cost.

2.1.14.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Conditions › Agroforestry
2.1.14.4.definition: Growing coffee among trees and other crops, which can support biodiversity and soil health.

2.1.14.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Conditions › Volcanic soils
2.1.14.5.definition: Fertile, well-draining soils of volcanic origin found in many coffee regions.

2.1.14.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Conditions › Distinct dry season
2.1.14.6.definition: A clear dry period that synchronizes coffee flowering and harvest.

2.1.14.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Conditions › Coffee belt (tropics)
2.1.14.7.definition: The band between roughly the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn where coffee is grown.

2.1.15.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Africa & Arabia
2.1.15.definition: Origins: Africa & Arabia is a group of 7 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Ethiopia (Yirgacheffe, Sidama, Guji), Kenya (Nyeri, Kirinyaga), Rwanda….

2.1.15.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Africa & Arabia › Ethiopia (Yirgacheffe, Sidama, Guji)
2.1.15.1.definition: Birthplace of Arabica, with diverse landraces; Yirgacheffe, Sidama and Guji are famous growing areas.

2.1.15.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Africa & Arabia › Kenya (Nyeri, Kirinyaga)
2.1.15.2.definition: Kenyan coffee regions known for bright, washed SL28 and SL34 coffees.

2.1.15.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Africa & Arabia › Rwanda
2.1.15.3.definition: East African producer of washed Bourbon-type coffees.

2.1.15.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Africa & Arabia › Burundi
2.1.15.4.definition: East African producer of washed Bourbon-type Arabicas.

2.1.15.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Africa & Arabia › Uganda
2.1.15.5.definition: Major African robusta producer, also growing Arabica.

2.1.15.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Africa & Arabia › Tanzania
2.1.15.6.definition: East African producer, including Kilimanjaro coffees.

2.1.15.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Africa & Arabia › Yemen
2.1.15.7.definition: Historic coffee origin with traditional natural-process coffee.

2.1.16.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America
2.1.16.definition: Origins: Latin America is a group of 11 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Colombia, Brazil, Guatemala….

2.1.16.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Colombia
2.1.16.1.definition: Major producer of washed Arabica, with harvests in most months across its regions.

2.1.16.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Brazil
2.1.16.2.definition: The world's largest coffee producer, known especially for natural and pulped-natural Arabicas, plus Conilon robusta.

2.1.16.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Guatemala
2.1.16.3.definition: Central American producer with distinct regions such as Antigua and Huehuetenango.

2.1.16.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Costa Rica
2.1.16.4.definition: Central American producer known for washed and honey coffees; growing only Arabica was long mandated by law.

2.1.16.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Honduras
2.1.16.5.definition: One of Central America's largest coffee producers.

2.1.16.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › El Salvador
2.1.16.6.definition: Central American producer known for Bourbon and the Pacas and Pacamara varieties.

2.1.16.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Panama
2.1.16.7.definition: Producer famous for Geisha coffees from Boquete.

2.1.16.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Peru
2.1.16.8.definition: Major producer of Arabica, including much certified organic coffee.

2.1.16.9.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Mexico
2.1.16.9.definition: Major producer, notable for organic coffee from Chiapas and Oaxaca.

2.1.16.10.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Nicaragua
2.1.16.10.definition: Central American producer, notably in Jinotega and Matagalpa.

2.1.16.11.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Latin America › Bolivia
2.1.16.11.definition: Small Andean coffee producer whose high-altitude farms are mainly in the Yungas.

2.1.17.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific
2.1.17.definition: Origins: Asia-Pacific is a group of 8 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Sumatra, Java, Sulawesi….

2.1.17.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific › Sumatra
2.1.17.1.definition: Indonesian island known for earthy, full-bodied, wet-hulled coffees.

2.1.17.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific › Java
2.1.17.2.definition: Indonesian island whose name became a byword for coffee; it grows both Arabica and robusta.

2.1.17.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific › Sulawesi

2.1.17.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific › Papua New Guinea

2.1.17.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific › India (Monsooned Malabar)
2.1.17.5.definition: Indian coffee exposed to monsoon winds, giving low acidity and an earthy flavor.

2.1.17.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific › Vietnam
2.1.17.6.definition: World's second-largest coffee producer, mostly robusta.

2.1.17.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific › Yunnan
2.1.17.7.definition: Chinese province that grows Arabica, mostly Catimor.

2.1.17.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Origins: Asia-Pacific › Hawaii (Kona)
2.1.17.8.definition: Coffee grown on the Kona slopes of Hawaii's Big Island.

2.1.18.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Harvest
2.1.18.definition: Harvest is a group of 5 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Production. It includes Selective hand-picking, Strip picking, Mechanical harvesting….

2.1.18.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Harvest › Selective hand-picking

2.1.18.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Harvest › Strip picking
2.1.18.2.definition: Harvesting all cherries from a branch at once.

2.1.18.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Harvest › Mechanical harvesting
2.1.18.3.definition: Machine-harvesting coffee from cherries on flat land, common in Brazil.

2.1.18.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Harvest › Ripeness sorting

2.1.18.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Harvest › Float sorting
2.1.18.5.definition: Putting cherries in water and removing floaters, which are often defective or underripe.

2.1.19.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Wet Processing Steps
2.1.19.definition: Wet Processing Steps is a group of 5 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Production. It includes Pulping, Fermentation (dry or underwater), Washing….

2.1.19.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Wet Processing Steps › Pulping
2.1.19.1.definition: Removing the cherry skin and fruit from coffee seeds.

2.1.19.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Wet Processing Steps › Fermentation (dry or underwater)
2.1.19.2.definition: Washed-process stage where microbes break down mucilage, either in dry tanks or under water.

2.1.19.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Wet Processing Steps › Washing
2.1.19.3.definition: Rinsing fermented coffee to remove remaining mucilage.

2.1.19.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Wet Processing Steps › Mechanical demucilaging
2.1.19.4.definition: Removing mucilage mechanically instead of by fermentation.

2.1.19.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Wet Processing Steps › Drying
2.1.19.5.definition: Reducing coffee moisture to a safe level for storage.

2.1.20.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Honey Grades
2.1.20.definition: Honey Grades is a group of 4 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Production. It includes White honey, Yellow honey, Red honey….

2.1.20.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Honey Grades › White honey

2.1.20.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Honey Grades › Yellow honey

2.1.20.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Honey Grades › Red honey

2.1.20.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Honey Grades › Black honey
2.1.20.4.definition: Honey process leaving the most mucilage and drying slowly, giving the most fruit-forward honey style.

2.1.21.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing
2.1.21.definition: Experimental Processing is a group of 8 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Production. It includes Anaerobic natural, Anaerobic washed, Carbonic maceration….

2.1.21.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing › Anaerobic natural
2.1.21.1.definition: Whole cherries fermented in sealed tanks, then dried as a natural.

2.1.21.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing › Anaerobic washed
2.1.21.2.definition: Coffee fermented in sealed tanks, then washed and dried.

2.1.21.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing › Carbonic maceration
2.1.21.3.definition: Whole, uncrushed grapes ferment inside a CO2-filled vessel, giving fruity, low-tannin reds (as in Beaujolais).

2.1.21.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing › Lactic process
2.1.21.4.definition: Fermentation method that encourages lactic acid bacteria to give creamy, yogurt-like notes.

2.1.21.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing › Yeast-inoculated
2.1.21.5.definition: Fermentation started with selected yeast strains.

2.1.21.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing › Thermal shock
2.1.21.6.definition: Rapid heat change during roasting or brewing.

2.1.21.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing › Co-fermented (infused)
2.1.21.7.definition: Coffee fermented with added fruit, spices or other ingredients. These flavors are not intrinsic to the coffee, so labeling transparency is debated.

2.1.21.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Experimental Processing › Double fermentation
2.1.21.8.definition: Fermenting coffee twice, e.g. Kenya's dry and then wet fermentation.

2.1.22.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Drying
2.1.22.definition: Drying is a group of 5 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Production. It includes Patio drying, Raised (African) beds, Mechanical dryers (guardiolas)….

2.1.22.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Drying › Patio drying
2.1.22.1.definition: Drying coffee spread on concrete or brick patios.

2.1.22.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Drying › Raised (African) beds
2.1.22.2.definition: Elevated mesh drying tables that improve airflow.

2.1.22.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Drying › Mechanical dryers (guardiolas)
2.1.22.3.definition: Rotating drum dryers used to dry coffee.

2.1.22.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Drying › Target moisture 10–12%
2.1.22.4.definition: Ideal moisture of dried green coffee for storage.

2.1.22.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Production › Drying › Resting (reposo)
2.1.22.5.definition: Letting dried coffee stabilize in parchment before milling.

2.1.23.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading
2.1.23.definition: Milling & Grading is a group of 8 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes Hulling (parchment removal), Polishing, Density sorting….

2.1.23.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading › Hulling (parchment removal)
2.1.23.1.definition: Removing the parchment layer (or dried husk) from green beans.

2.1.23.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading › Polishing
2.1.23.2.definition: Removing the silverskin from green beans for appearance.

2.1.23.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading › Density sorting
2.1.23.3.definition: Separating beans by density, since denser beans are often higher quality.

2.1.23.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading › Optical color sorting
2.1.23.4.definition: Machines that reject beans by color.

2.1.23.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading › Screen size grading
2.1.23.5.definition: Grading beans by size using sieves numbered in 64ths of an inch.

2.1.23.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading › SCA specialty grade
2.1.23.6.definition: Green coffee with zero primary defects, few secondary defects and a cupping score of 80+.

2.1.23.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading › Primary defects (black, sour, fungus)
2.1.23.7.definition: Serious green-coffee defects counted more heavily in grading.

2.1.23.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Milling & Grading › Secondary defects (broken, insect, quakers)
2.1.23.8.definition: Less severe green-coffee defects, such as broken beans, insect damage and unripe 'quakers'.

2.1.24.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Roast Chemistry
2.1.24.definition: Roast Chemistry is a group of 6 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Science. It includes Drying phase, Maillard reactions, Caramelization….

2.1.24.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Roast Chemistry › Drying phase
2.1.24.1.definition: Early roasting stage in which moisture evaporates.

2.1.24.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Roast Chemistry › Maillard reactions
2.1.24.2.definition: Browning reactions between sugars and amino acids that create roasted flavors and color.

2.1.24.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Roast Chemistry › Caramelization
2.1.24.3.definition: Browning of sugars by heat during roasting.

2.1.24.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Roast Chemistry › Strecker degradation
2.1.24.4.definition: Roasting reaction of amino acids that produces aroma compounds.

2.1.24.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Roast Chemistry › Chlorogenic acid breakdown
2.1.24.5.definition: Roasting breaks down chlorogenic acids, reducing their bitter, astringent contribution.

2.1.24.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Roast Chemistry › CO2 degassing
2.1.24.6.definition: Roasted coffee releasing carbon dioxide over the days after roasting.

2.1.25.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Roast Profile
2.1.25.definition: Roast Profile is a group of 7 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Techniques. It includes Charge temperature, Turning point, Rate of rise (RoR)….

2.1.25.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Roast Profile › Charge temperature
2.1.25.1.definition: Roaster temperature when the green beans are dropped in.

2.1.25.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Roast Profile › Turning point
2.1.25.2.definition: Lowest probe temperature after beans are charged into the roaster.

2.1.25.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Roast Profile › Rate of rise (RoR)
2.1.25.3.definition: Speed at which bean temperature increases during roasting.

2.1.25.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Roast Profile › First crack
2.1.25.4.definition: Audible popping during roasting as moisture and gases escape; marks the start of a light roast.

2.1.25.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Roast Profile › Development time ratio
2.1.25.5.definition: Share of total roast time after first crack.

2.1.25.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Roast Profile › Second crack
2.1.25.6.definition: Later cracking during roasting, associated with darker roasts.

2.1.25.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Roast Profile › Agtron color
2.1.25.7.definition: Roast-color measurement made with Agtron infrared devices; higher numbers mean lighter roasts.

2.1.26.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Extraction & Strength
2.1.26.definition: Extraction & Strength is a group of 5 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Science. It includes Extraction yield (18–22%), Total dissolved solids (TDS), SCA brewing control chart….

2.1.26.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Extraction & Strength › Extraction yield (18–22%)
2.1.26.1.definition: Share of the dry coffee's mass dissolved into the brew; the SCA ideal range is about 18–22%.

2.1.26.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Extraction & Strength › Total dissolved solids (TDS)
2.1.26.2.definition: Total amount of dissolved minerals and salts in water, usually in mg/L.

2.1.26.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Extraction & Strength › SCA brewing control chart
2.1.26.3.definition: Chart relating extraction yield and brew strength (TDS) to define balanced coffee.

2.1.26.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Extraction & Strength › Brew ratio (~1:15–1:18)
2.1.26.4.definition: Ratio of coffee to water; filter coffee commonly uses about 1 g of coffee per 15–18 g of water.

2.1.26.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Extraction & Strength › Refractometer
2.1.26.5.definition: Instrument that measures dissolved solids (TDS) in brewed coffee.

2.1.27.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Brewing Variables
2.1.27.definition: Brewing Variables is a group of 7 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Techniques. It includes Grind size, Water temperature (90–96 °C), Contact time….

2.1.27.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Brewing Variables › Grind size
2.1.27.1.definition: Particle size of ground coffee, matched to the brewing method.

2.1.27.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Brewing Variables › Water temperature (90–96 °C)

2.1.27.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Brewing Variables › Contact time
2.1.27.3.definition: How long water and coffee are in contact during brewing.

2.1.27.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Brewing Variables › Agitation
2.1.27.4.definition: Stirring or turbulence during brewing; more agitation speeds up extraction.

2.1.27.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Brewing Variables › Bypass
2.1.27.5.definition: Water added to brewed coffee after extraction to dilute it, used in some batch brewers.

2.1.27.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Brewing Variables › Espresso ratio (~1:2)
2.1.27.6.definition: A common espresso recipe uses about twice as much liquid out as dry coffee in.

2.1.27.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Techniques › Brewing Variables › Pressure (~9 bar)

2.1.28.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Water for Coffee
2.1.28.definition: Water for Coffee is a group of 5 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Science. It includes SCA water standard (TDS ~150 mg/L), Calcium hardness, Alkalinity (~40 mg/L)….

2.1.28.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Water for Coffee › SCA water standard (TDS ~150 mg/L)
2.1.28.1.definition: SCA target water chemistry for brewing, with TDS around 150 mg/L.

2.1.28.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Water for Coffee › Calcium hardness
2.1.28.2.definition: Calcium in brewing water, which affects extraction and scale formation.

2.1.28.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Water for Coffee › Alkalinity (~40 mg/L)
2.1.28.3.definition: Water's buffering capacity (bicarbonate). SCA guidance targets about 40 mg/L as CaCO3 so acidity is not dulled.

2.1.28.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Water for Coffee › pH ~7
2.1.28.4.definition: Neutral pH target for brewing water.

2.1.28.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Science › Water for Coffee › Chlorine-free
2.1.28.5.definition: Brewing water free of chlorine, which would otherwise cause off-flavors.

2.1.29.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol
2.1.29.definition: Cupping Protocol is a group of 12 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes SCA cupping form, Fragrance/aroma, Flavor….

2.1.29.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › SCA cupping form
2.1.29.1.definition: Specialty Coffee Association scoring sheet for evaluating coffee quality.

2.1.29.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Fragrance/aroma
2.1.29.2.definition: Cupping attribute: smell of the dry grounds (fragrance) and wet coffee (aroma).

2.1.29.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Flavor
2.1.29.3.definition: Cupping attribute: combined taste and retronasal aroma.

2.1.29.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Aftertaste
2.1.29.4.definition: Cupping attribute: the length and quality of the flavors left after swallowing.

2.1.29.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Acidity
2.1.29.5.definition: Cupping attribute for perceived brightness or tartness (e.g. citric, malic), valued in many specialty coffees.

2.1.29.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Body
2.1.29.6.definition: Cupping attribute for the weight and texture of coffee in the mouth.

2.1.29.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Balance
2.1.29.7.definition: Cupping attribute: how well flavor, acidity, body and aftertaste fit together.

2.1.29.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Uniformity
2.1.29.8.definition: Cupping attribute for consistency across cups of the same sample.

2.1.29.9.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Clean cup
2.1.29.9.definition: Cupping attribute: no taints or defects from first sip to aftertaste.

2.1.29.10.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Sweetness

2.1.29.11.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Overall
2.1.29.11.definition: Cupping score reflecting the cupper's holistic impression.

2.1.29.12.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Cupping Protocol › Specialty = 80+ points
2.1.29.12.definition: Under SCA grading, coffee scoring 80 points or above qualifies as specialty grade.

2.1.30.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR)
2.1.30.definition: Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) is a group of 9 entries in the Coffee Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes Fruity, Floral, Sweet….

2.1.30.1.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Fruity
2.1.30.1.definition: Flavor category including berry, citrus and stone-fruit notes.

2.1.30.2.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Floral
2.1.30.2.definition: Flavor category with notes such as jasmine, rose and other flowers.

2.1.30.3.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Sweet

2.1.30.4.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Nutty/cocoa
2.1.30.4.definition: Flavor category with nut and chocolate notes.

2.1.30.5.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Spices

2.1.30.6.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Roasted
2.1.30.6.definition: Coffee after roasting, ready to grind and brew.

2.1.30.7.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Green/vegetative
2.1.30.7.definition: Flavor category with fresh, herbal or underdeveloped notes.

2.1.30.8.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Sour/fermented
2.1.30.8.definition: Flavor category for sour or fermented notes.

2.1.30.9.path: Steep Guild › Coffee Academy › Quality & Standards › Flavor Wheel (SCA/WCR) › Other (papery, chemical)
2.1.30.9.definition: Flavor-wheel category for off-flavors such as papery, chemical or musty.

2.2.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › White Tea
2.2.1.definition: White Tea is a group of 4 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Silver Needle (Bai Hao Yin Zhen), White Peony (Bai Mu Dan), Shou Mei….

2.2.1.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › White Tea › Silver Needle (Bai Hao Yin Zhen)
2.2.1.1.definition: Chinese white tea made only from unopened buds.

2.2.1.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › White Tea › White Peony (Bai Mu Dan)
2.2.1.2.definition: White tea made from buds and young leaves.

2.2.1.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › White Tea › Shou Mei
2.2.1.3.definition: Chinese white tea from later, larger leaves.

2.2.1.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › White Tea › Darjeeling white
2.2.1.4.definition: White tea made in Darjeeling, India.

2.2.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Yellow Tea
2.2.2.definition: Yellow Tea is a group of 3 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Junshan Yinzhen, Meng Ding Huang Ya, Huoshan Huang Ya.

2.2.2.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Yellow Tea › Junshan Yinzhen
2.2.2.1.definition: Yellow tea from Junshan Island in Hunan.

2.2.2.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Yellow Tea › Meng Ding Huang Ya
2.2.2.2.definition: Yellow tea from Mount Meng, Sichuan.

2.2.2.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Yellow Tea › Huoshan Huang Ya

2.2.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea
2.2.3.definition: Green Tea is a group of 9 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Longjing (Dragon Well), Bi Luo Chun, Gunpowder….

2.2.3.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Longjing (Dragon Well)
2.2.3.1.definition: Flat, pan-fired green tea from Hangzhou, Zhejiang.

2.2.3.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Bi Luo Chun
2.2.3.2.definition: Famous Chinese green tea from the Dongting mountains near Suzhou, Jiangsu, rolled into tight spirals.

2.2.3.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Gunpowder
2.2.3.3.definition: Chinese green tea rolled into small pellets.

2.2.3.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Sencha
2.2.3.4.definition: Steamed Japanese green tea, the most common tea in Japan.

2.2.3.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Gyokuro
2.2.3.5.definition: Japanese green tea shaded for about three weeks before harvest, giving sweet, savory flavor.

2.2.3.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Matcha
2.2.3.6.definition: Finely stone-ground powder of shade-grown Japanese tencha leaf, whisked into water.

2.2.3.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Hojicha

2.2.3.8.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Genmaicha
2.2.3.8.definition: Japanese green tea blended with roasted rice.

2.2.3.9.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Green Tea › Bancha
2.2.3.9.definition: Everyday Japanese green tea from later harvests and larger leaves.

2.2.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Oolong Tea
2.2.4.definition: Oolong Tea is a group of 6 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Tieguanyin, Da Hong Pao (Wuyi rock), Dong Ding….

2.2.4.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Oolong Tea › Tieguanyin
2.2.4.1.definition: Famous Chinese oolong from Anxi, Fujian.

2.2.4.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Oolong Tea › Da Hong Pao (Wuyi rock)
2.2.4.2.definition: Famous Wuyi rock oolong from Fujian.

2.2.4.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Oolong Tea › Dong Ding
2.2.4.3.definition: Roasted rolled oolong from Lugu, Nantou, Taiwan.

2.2.4.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Oolong Tea › Alishan high-mountain
2.2.4.4.definition: Taiwanese high-mountain oolong from the Alishan area of Chiayi.

2.2.4.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Oolong Tea › Oriental Beauty
2.2.4.5.definition: Taiwanese oolong made from leaves bitten by leafhoppers, giving honey-like notes.

2.2.4.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Oolong Tea › Dan Cong
2.2.4.6.definition: Guangdong oolongs from Phoenix Mountain, known for aromas resembling flowers and fruit.

2.2.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea
2.2.5.definition: Black Tea is a group of 8 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Assam, Darjeeling, Ceylon….

2.2.5.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea › Assam
2.2.5.1.definition: Tea from Assam, India, typically strong and malty, from var. assamica plants.

2.2.5.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea › Darjeeling
2.2.5.2.definition: Tea from the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, India.

2.2.5.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea › Ceylon
2.2.5.3.definition: Tea from Sri Lanka, named after the island's former name.

2.2.5.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea › Keemun
2.2.5.4.definition: Chinese black tea from Qimen, Anhui.

2.2.5.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea › Dian Hong (Yunnan)
2.2.5.5.definition: Yunnan black tea, often rich in golden buds.

2.2.5.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea › Lapsang Souchong
2.2.5.6.definition: Chinese black tea from Wuyi, often smoked over pinewood.

2.2.5.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea › English Breakfast blend
2.2.5.7.definition: Robust black tea blend, often of Assam, Ceylon and Kenyan teas.

2.2.5.8.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Black Tea › Earl Grey
2.2.5.8.definition: Black tea flavored with bergamot oil.

2.2.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Dark Tea
2.2.6.definition: Dark Tea is a group of 4 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Sheng (raw) pu-erh, Shou (ripe) pu-erh, Liu Bao….

2.2.6.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Dark Tea › Sheng (raw) pu-erh
2.2.6.1.definition: Pu-erh tea pressed and aged slowly without accelerated fermentation.

2.2.6.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Dark Tea › Shou (ripe) pu-erh
2.2.6.2.definition: Pu-erh tea whose aging is accelerated by wet piling (wo dui).

2.2.6.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Dark Tea › Liu Bao

2.2.6.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Dark Tea › Fu Zhuan (Anhua brick)
2.2.6.4.definition: Dark brick tea from Anhua, Hunan, known for its 'golden flower' fungus.

2.2.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Herbal Tisanes
2.2.7.definition: Herbal Tisanes is a group of 7 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Rooibos, Honeybush, Chamomile….

2.2.7.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Herbal Tisanes › Rooibos
2.2.7.1.definition: Caffeine-free South African herbal infusion from Aspalathus linearis.

2.2.7.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Herbal Tisanes › Honeybush
2.2.7.2.definition: Caffeine-free South African infusion from Cyclopia species.

2.2.7.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Herbal Tisanes › Chamomile
2.2.7.3.definition: Caffeine-free herbal infusion of chamomile flowers.

2.2.7.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Herbal Tisanes › Peppermint

2.2.7.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Herbal Tisanes › Hibiscus
2.2.7.5.definition: Tart, red, caffeine-free infusion of hibiscus calyces.

2.2.7.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Herbal Tisanes › Ginger
2.2.7.6.definition: Rhizome used for spicy herbal infusions and in chai.

2.2.7.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Herbal Tisanes › Lemongrass

2.2.8.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Scented & Blended
2.2.8.definition: Scented & Blended is a group of 6 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Jasmine tea, Earl Grey (bergamot), Lychee black….

2.2.8.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Scented & Blended › Jasmine tea
2.2.8.1.definition: Tea, usually green, scented with jasmine blossoms.

2.2.8.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Scented & Blended › Earl Grey (bergamot)
2.2.8.2.definition: Black tea flavored with bergamot oil.

2.2.8.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Scented & Blended › Lychee black
2.2.8.3.definition: Black tea flavored or scented with lychee.

2.2.8.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Scented & Blended › Rose black

2.2.8.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Scented & Blended › Osmanthus oolong

2.2.8.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Scented & Blended › Chai spice blend
2.2.8.6.definition: Spices such as cardamom, ginger, cinnamon, clove and black pepper used in chai.

2.2.9.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Drinks
2.2.9.definition: Tea Drinks is a group of 7 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Iced tea, Sweet tea (US South), Milk tea….

2.2.9.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Drinks › Iced tea
2.2.9.1.definition: Brewed tea served chilled over ice.

2.2.9.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Drinks › Sweet tea (US South)

2.2.9.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Drinks › Milk tea
2.2.9.3.definition: Tea brewed and served with milk.

2.2.9.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Drinks › Chai latte
2.2.9.4.definition: Spiced tea concentrate mixed with steamed milk.

2.2.9.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Drinks › Matcha latte

2.2.9.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Drinks › London fog
2.2.9.6.definition: Earl Grey latte with vanilla and steamed milk.

2.2.9.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Drinks › Arnold Palmer (tea + lemonade)
2.2.9.7.definition: Drink of iced tea mixed with lemonade, named after the golfer.

2.2.10.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Formats
2.2.10.definition: Tea Formats is a group of 6 entries in the Tea Academy. It includes Loose leaf, Tea bags, Pyramid sachets….

2.2.10.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Formats › Loose leaf

2.2.10.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Formats › Tea bags
2.2.10.2.definition: Portioned tea in paper or mesh bags.

2.2.10.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Formats › Pyramid sachets
2.2.10.3.definition: Tetrahedral tea bags that give leaves more room to expand.

2.2.10.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Formats › Compressed cakes/bricks
2.2.10.4.definition: Tea pressed into cakes or bricks, traditional for pu-erh and other dark teas.

2.2.10.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Formats › Powdered (matcha/instant)
2.2.10.5.definition: Tea as a fine powder, either ground leaf or soluble.

2.2.10.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Tea Formats › RTD bottled tea

2.2.11.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Tea Plant Varieties
2.2.11.definition: Tea Plant Varieties is a group of 3 entries in the Tea Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Camellia sinensis var. sinensis, Camellia sinensis var. assamica, Cambod (hybrid type).

2.2.11.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Tea Plant Varieties › Camellia sinensis var. sinensis
2.2.11.1.definition: Small-leaf, cold-tolerant tea plant variety of China and Japan.

2.2.11.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Tea Plant Varieties › Camellia sinensis var. assamica
2.2.11.2.definition: Large-leaf tea plant variety native to Assam and Yunnan, used for strong black teas and pu-erh.

2.2.11.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Tea Plant Varieties › Cambod (hybrid type)
2.2.11.3.definition: Cambod-type tea plant, a third main tea plant type with intermediate traits, alongside China and Assam types.

2.2.12.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars
2.2.12.definition: Notable Cultivars is a group of 12 entries in the Tea Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Yabukita, Okumidori, Saemidori….

2.2.12.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Yabukita

2.2.12.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Okumidori

2.2.12.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Saemidori
2.2.12.3.definition: Japanese tea cultivar with sweet, vivid-green tea.

2.2.12.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Asatsuyu
2.2.12.4.definition: Japanese tea cultivar known for natural sweetness.

2.2.12.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Fuding Da Bai
2.2.12.5.definition: Tea cultivar from Fuding, Fujian, widely used for white tea.

2.2.12.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Tieguanyin
2.2.12.6.definition: Famous Chinese oolong from Anxi, Fujian.

2.2.12.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Jin Xuan (TTES #12)
2.2.12.7.definition: Taiwanese oolong cultivar known for creamy, 'milky' notes.

2.2.12.8.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Qing Xin

2.2.12.9.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Rou Gui
2.2.12.9.definition: Wuyi rock oolong cultivar with a cinnamon-like aroma.

2.2.12.10.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Shui Xian

2.2.12.11.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › Longjing #43
2.2.12.11.definition: Longjing tea cultivar bred for early budding.

2.2.12.12.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Notable Cultivars › AV2 (Darjeeling clone)
2.2.12.12.definition: Clonal tea cultivar developed at Ambari Tea Estate and widely planted in Darjeeling.

2.2.13.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions
2.2.13.definition: Growing Regions is a group of 8 entries in the Tea Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes China (Fujian, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Anhui), India (Darjeeling, Assam, Nilgiri), Sri Lanka (Nuwara Eliya, Uva, Dimbula)….

2.2.13.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions › China (Fujian, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Anhui)
2.2.13.1.definition: Main Chinese tea provinces, home to many famous teas.

2.2.13.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions › India (Darjeeling, Assam, Nilgiri)

2.2.13.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions › Sri Lanka (Nuwara Eliya, Uva, Dimbula)

2.2.13.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions › Japan (Shizuoka, Uji, Kagoshima)
2.2.13.4.definition: Main Japanese tea regions; Shizuoka is the largest producer.

2.2.13.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions › Taiwan (Alishan, Nantou)

2.2.13.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions › Kenya
2.2.13.6.definition: Major black tea producer, mostly CTC.

2.2.13.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions › Nepal (Ilam)

2.2.13.8.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Regions › Vietnam
2.2.13.8.definition: Tea producer known for green and black tea.

2.2.14.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Practices
2.2.14.definition: Growing Practices is a group of 6 entries in the Tea Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Elevation, Shading (kabuse, tencha), Seasonal flushes (first, second, autumn)….

2.2.14.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Practices › Elevation
2.2.14.1.definition: Garden altitude; higher elevations often give slower growth and more aromatic tea.

2.2.14.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Practices › Shading (kabuse, tencha)
2.2.14.2.definition: Covering tea plants before harvest; kabuse is shaded sencha, and tencha is shaded leaf for matcha.

2.2.14.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Practices › Seasonal flushes (first, second, autumn)
2.2.14.3.definition: Harvest periods of new growth; Darjeeling first and second flushes are famous.

2.2.14.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Practices › Plucking table pruning
2.2.14.4.definition: Pruning tea bushes flat for an even plucking surface.

2.2.14.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Practices › Organic/biodynamic
2.2.14.5.definition: Tea grown under organic or biodynamic certification.

2.2.14.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Growing Practices › Old-tree (gushu) gardens
2.2.14.6.definition: Gardens of old tea trees, prized in Yunnan for pu-erh.

2.2.15.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Plucking Standards
2.2.15.definition: Plucking Standards is a group of 5 entries in the Tea Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Bud only, One bud, one leaf, One bud, two leaves….

2.2.15.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Plucking Standards › Bud only
2.2.15.1.definition: Plucking only the unopened bud, as for Silver Needle.

2.2.15.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Plucking Standards › One bud, one leaf
2.2.15.2.definition: Fine plucking standard: the bud plus the first leaf.

2.2.15.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Plucking Standards › One bud, two leaves
2.2.15.3.definition: Classic plucking standard: the bud plus two leaves.

2.2.15.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Plucking Standards › One bud, three leaves
2.2.15.4.definition: Coarser plucking standard: the bud plus three leaves.

2.2.15.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Plucking Standards › Mature leaves (oolong, dark tea)
2.2.15.5.definition: Larger, more mature leaves used for oolong and dark teas.

2.2.16.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps
2.2.16.definition: Processing Steps is a group of 8 entries in the Tea Academy, under Production. It includes Withering, Bruising/shaking (oolong), Rolling….

2.2.16.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Withering
2.2.16.1.definition: Letting fresh tea leaves lose moisture and soften before rolling.

2.2.16.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Bruising/shaking (oolong)
2.2.16.2.definition: Tossing oolong leaves to bruise their edges and start partial oxidation.

2.2.16.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Rolling
2.2.16.3.definition: Shaping tea leaves and breaking their cells to release juices.

2.2.16.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Oxidation
2.2.16.4.definition: Enzymatic browning of tea leaves after bruising; full oxidation makes black tea.

2.2.16.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Kill-green (sha qing)
2.2.16.5.definition: Heating fresh tea leaves to stop oxidation, used for green and some other teas.

2.2.16.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Drying/firing
2.2.16.6.definition: Final heating that removes moisture and fixes tea's flavor.

2.2.16.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Sorting
2.2.16.7.definition: Separating tea by leaf size and quality.

2.2.16.8.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Roasting
2.2.16.8.definition: Heating tea to develop toasty flavors.

2.2.17.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Kill-Green Methods
2.2.17.definition: Kill-Green Methods is a group of 4 entries in the Tea Academy, under Production. It includes Pan-firing (wok), Steaming (Japan), Baking….

2.2.17.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Kill-Green Methods › Pan-firing (wok)
2.2.17.1.definition: Kill-green by heating leaves in a pan or wok, typical of Chinese green tea.

2.2.17.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Kill-Green Methods › Steaming (Japan)

2.2.17.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Kill-Green Methods › Baking
2.2.17.3.definition: Heating tea leaves (for example oolong) to dry them and develop toasty flavor.

2.2.17.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Kill-Green Methods › Sun-drying (pu-erh maocha)
2.2.17.4.definition: Sun-drying pu-erh leaves to make maocha (raw material tea).

2.2.18.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Process by Tea Type
2.2.18.definition: Process by Tea Type is a group of 6 entries in the Tea Academy, under Production. It includes White: wither + dry, Yellow: kill-green + yellowing (men huang), Green: kill-green + roll + dry….

2.2.18.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Process by Tea Type › White: wither + dry
2.2.18.1.definition: White tea is minimally processed: withered and dried.

2.2.18.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Process by Tea Type › Yellow: kill-green + yellowing (men huang)
2.2.18.2.definition: Yellow tea gets a 'sealed yellowing' step (men huang) after kill-green.

2.2.18.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Process by Tea Type › Green: kill-green + roll + dry
2.2.18.3.definition: Green tea is heated to stop oxidation, then rolled and dried.

2.2.18.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Process by Tea Type › Oolong: partial oxidation
2.2.18.4.definition: Partially oxidized tea, between green and black.

2.2.18.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Process by Tea Type › Black: full oxidation
2.2.18.5.definition: Black tea is fully oxidized after withering and rolling.

2.2.18.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Process by Tea Type › Dark: heaping (wo dui) / aging
2.2.18.6.definition: Dark tea is made by piling damp leaves to ferment microbially (wo dui), or by long aging.

2.2.19.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Post-Processing
2.2.19.definition: Post-Processing is a group of 5 entries in the Tea Academy, under Production. It includes Compression (cakes, bricks), Aging, Re-roasting….

2.2.19.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Post-Processing › Compression (cakes, bricks)
2.2.19.1.definition: Steaming and pressing tea into cakes or bricks.

2.2.19.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Post-Processing › Aging
2.2.19.2.definition: Storing tea, especially pu-erh, other dark teas, white tea and some oolongs, for months to years so its flavor develops.

2.2.19.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Post-Processing › Re-roasting
2.2.19.3.definition: Roasting tea again to refresh it or change its character.

2.2.19.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Post-Processing › Scenting (jasmine)
2.2.19.4.definition: Layering tea with fresh flowers so it absorbs their aroma.

2.2.19.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Post-Processing › Blending
2.2.19.5.definition: Combining teas from different gardens or origins for a consistent flavor.

2.2.20.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing
2.2.20.definition: Japanese Processing is a group of 9 entries in the Tea Academy, under Production. It includes Aracha (crude tea), Asamushi (light steam), Fukamushi (deep steam)….

2.2.20.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Aracha (crude tea)
2.2.20.1.definition: Japanese green tea after primary processing, before it is sorted and refined.

2.2.20.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Asamushi (light steam)
2.2.20.2.definition: Japanese sencha steamed briefly (lightly), keeping leaves more intact.

2.2.20.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Fukamushi (deep steam)
2.2.20.3.definition: Japanese sencha steamed longer, giving a deeper green, fuller brew.

2.2.20.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Tencha (for matcha)
2.2.20.4.definition: Shaded, steamed and dried tea leaf with stems and veins removed, ground into matcha.

2.2.20.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Stone-milling
2.2.20.5.definition: Grinding tencha in granite mills to make matcha.

2.2.20.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Gyokuro shading (~3 weeks)
2.2.20.6.definition: Shading tea plants for about three weeks before harvest to raise amino acids and sweetness.

2.2.20.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Hojicha roasting
2.2.20.7.definition: Roasting green tea, including stems, at high heat to make hojicha.

2.2.20.8.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Kukicha (stems)
2.2.20.8.definition: Japanese tea made from stems and twigs.

2.2.20.9.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Japanese Processing › Shiage (refining)
2.2.20.9.definition: Japanese finishing step that sorts and fires aracha.

2.2.21.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Orthodox vs CTC
2.2.21.definition: Orthodox vs CTC is a group of 5 entries in the Tea Academy, under Production. It includes Orthodox rolling, CTC (crush, tear, curl), Rotorvane….

2.2.21.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Orthodox vs CTC › Orthodox rolling
2.2.21.1.definition: Traditional rolling that keeps leaves whole or broken, rather than CTC.

2.2.21.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Orthodox vs CTC › CTC (crush, tear, curl)
2.2.21.2.definition: 'Crush, tear, curl' machine processing that produces small granules for strong, fast-brewing tea.

2.2.21.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Orthodox vs CTC › Rotorvane
2.2.21.3.definition: Machine that cuts withered leaf, used before or instead of CTC.

2.2.21.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Orthodox vs CTC › Fannings
2.2.21.4.definition: Small broken tea particles, larger than dust, used in tea bags.

2.2.21.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Production › Orthodox vs CTC › Dust
2.2.21.5.definition: Smallest tea particle grade, used in tea bags.

2.2.22.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades
2.2.22.definition: Leaf Grades is a group of 10 entries in the Tea Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes OP (Orange Pekoe), FOP, GFOP….

2.2.22.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › OP (Orange Pekoe)
2.2.22.1.definition: Leaf grade term for whole-leaf black tea; it does not refer to orange flavor.

2.2.22.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › FOP
2.2.22.2.definition: Flowery Orange Pekoe: whole-leaf grade with some tips.

2.2.22.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › GFOP
2.2.22.3.definition: Golden Flowery Orange Pekoe: whole-leaf grade with golden tips.

2.2.22.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › TGFOP
2.2.22.4.definition: Tippy Golden Flowery Orange Pekoe: whole-leaf grade with many golden tips.

2.2.22.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › FTGFOP
2.2.22.5.definition: Finest Tippy Golden Flowery Orange Pekoe: high whole-leaf grade with many tips, used in Darjeeling and Assam.

2.2.22.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › SFTGFOP
2.2.22.6.definition: Special Finest Tippy Golden Flowery Orange Pekoe, a top whole-leaf grade.

2.2.22.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › BOP (Broken OP)
2.2.22.7.definition: Leaf grade: broken orange pekoe, smaller leaf pieces than whole-leaf OP.

2.2.22.8.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › Fannings
2.2.22.8.definition: Small broken tea particles, larger than dust, used in tea bags.

2.2.22.9.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › Dust
2.2.22.9.definition: Smallest tea particle grade, used in tea bags.

2.2.22.10.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Quality & Standards › Leaf Grades › CTC grades (BP, PD)
2.2.22.10.definition: Grade names for granular CTC tea, such as Broken Pekoe and Pekoe Dust.

2.2.23.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Methods
2.2.23.definition: Brewing Methods is a group of 6 entries in the Tea Academy, under Techniques. It includes Western teapot, Gongfu cha (gaiwan, Yixing), Grandpa style….

2.2.23.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Methods › Western teapot
2.2.23.1.definition: Larger pot with fewer, longer infusions.

2.2.23.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Methods › Gongfu cha (gaiwan, Yixing)
2.2.23.2.definition: Chinese brewing style using a high leaf-to-water ratio and many short infusions, in a gaiwan or Yixing clay pot.

2.2.23.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Methods › Grandpa style
2.2.23.3.definition: Leaves steeped loose in a glass and topped up with water as you drink.

2.2.23.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Methods › Kyusu (Japanese)
2.2.23.4.definition: Japanese teapot, often with a side handle.

2.2.23.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Methods › Cold brew
2.2.23.5.definition: Coffee extracted with cold or room-temperature water over many hours.

2.2.23.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Methods › Matcha whisking (chasen)
2.2.23.6.definition: Whisking matcha with a bamboo whisk to make a frothy tea.

2.2.24.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Parameters
2.2.24.definition: Brewing Parameters is a group of 7 entries in the Tea Academy, under Techniques. It includes White/green ~70–85 °C, Oolong ~85–95 °C, Black/dark ~95–100 °C….

2.2.24.1.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Parameters › White/green ~70–85 °C
2.2.24.1.definition: Typical water temperature for white and green teas.

2.2.24.2.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Parameters › Oolong ~85–95 °C

2.2.24.3.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Parameters › Black/dark ~95–100 °C
2.2.24.3.definition: Typical near-boiling water temperature for black and dark teas.

2.2.24.4.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Parameters › Western ~2–3 g per 250 mL
2.2.24.4.definition: Typical leaf ratio for Western-style brewing.

2.2.24.5.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Parameters › Gongfu ~5–7 g per 100 mL

2.2.24.6.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Parameters › Multiple infusions
2.2.24.6.definition: Re-steeping the same leaves several times.

2.2.24.7.path: Steep Guild › Tea Academy › Techniques › Brewing Parameters › Soft water
2.2.24.7.definition: Low-mineral water, preferred for brewing delicate teas.

2.3.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Culture & Fermentation
2.3.1.definition: Culture & Fermentation is a group of 4 entries in the Kombucha Academy. It includes SCOBY (bacterial cellulose pellicle), Starter liquid (backslopping), Primary fermentation (F1)….

2.3.1.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Culture & Fermentation › SCOBY (bacterial cellulose pellicle)
2.3.1.1.definition: 'Symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeast', the cellulose mat that ferments kombucha.

2.3.1.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Culture & Fermentation › Starter liquid (backslopping)
2.3.1.2.definition: Using mature kombucha from a previous batch to acidify and inoculate a new one.

2.3.1.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Culture & Fermentation › Primary fermentation (F1)
2.3.1.3.definition: First open fermentation of sweet tea with the SCOBY and starter liquid.

2.3.1.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Culture & Fermentation › Secondary fermentation (F2, bottle conditioning)

2.3.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Base Teas
2.3.2.definition: Base Teas is a group of 5 entries in the Kombucha Academy. It includes Black tea kombucha, Green tea kombucha, Oolong kombucha….

2.3.2.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Base Teas › Black tea kombucha
2.3.2.1.definition: Kombucha brewed on black tea, the traditional base.

2.3.2.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Base Teas › Green tea kombucha

2.3.2.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Base Teas › Oolong kombucha

2.3.2.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Base Teas › White tea kombucha

2.3.2.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Base Teas › Herbal/rooibos-base kombucha
2.3.2.5.definition: Kombucha brewed on rooibos or herbal infusions instead of Camellia sinensis tea.

2.3.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Kombucha Styles
2.3.3.definition: Kombucha Styles is a group of 5 entries in the Kombucha Academy. It includes Original/plain, Fruit-flavored, Ginger….

2.3.3.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Kombucha Styles › Original/plain

2.3.3.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Kombucha Styles › Fruit-flavored

2.3.3.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Kombucha Styles › Ginger

2.3.3.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Kombucha Styles › Botanical/herbal
2.3.3.4.definition: Kombucha flavored with herbs or botanicals.

2.3.3.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Kombucha Styles › Hard kombucha (>0.5% ABV)
2.3.3.5.definition: Kombucha intentionally fermented to higher alcohol.

2.3.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Related Cultures
2.3.4.definition: Related Cultures is a group of 2 entries in the Kombucha Academy. It includes Jun (green tea and honey), Kombucha vinegar.

2.3.4.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Related Cultures › Jun (green tea and honey)
2.3.4.1.definition: Kombucha-like ferment made with green tea and honey.

2.3.4.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Related Cultures › Kombucha vinegar
2.3.4.2.definition: Kombucha fermented long enough to become very acidic, like vinegar.

2.3.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes
2.3.5.definition: SCOBY Microbes is a group of 8 entries in the Kombucha Academy, under Science. It includes Komagataeibacter xylinus, Acetobacter, Gluconobacter….

2.3.5.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes › Komagataeibacter xylinus
2.3.5.1.definition: Bacterium (formerly Acetobacter/Gluconacetobacter xylinus) that produces the cellulose pellicle.

2.3.5.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes › Acetobacter
2.3.5.2.definition: Genus of acetic acid bacteria that turn ethanol into acetic acid in kombucha and vinegar.

2.3.5.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes › Gluconobacter
2.3.5.3.definition: Acetic acid bacteria genus often found in kombucha cultures.

2.3.5.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes › Brettanomyces (Dekkera)
2.3.5.4.definition: Wild yeast genus giving 'funky', earthy or fruity flavors; prized in some beers, a fault in most wines.

2.3.5.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes › Zygosaccharomyces
2.3.5.5.definition: Acid-tolerant yeast genus common in kombucha.

2.3.5.6.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes › Saccharomyces
2.3.5.6.definition: Yeast genus commonly found in kombucha.

2.3.5.7.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes › Schizosaccharomyces
2.3.5.7.definition: Fission yeast genus sometimes found in kombucha.

2.3.5.8.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Microbes › Lactobacillus (variable)
2.3.5.8.definition: Lactic acid bacteria found in some kombucha cultures, in varying amounts.

2.3.6.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Biology
2.3.6.definition: SCOBY Biology is a group of 5 entries in the Kombucha Academy, under Science. It includes Bacterial cellulose pellicle, Yeast invertase splits sucrose, Yeast make ethanol….

2.3.6.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Biology › Bacterial cellulose pellicle
2.3.6.1.definition: The rubbery mat formed by bacteria such as Komagataeibacter; often called the SCOBY.

2.3.6.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Biology › Yeast invertase splits sucrose
2.3.6.2.definition: Yeast enzymes split sugar into glucose and fructose.

2.3.6.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Biology › Yeast make ethanol
2.3.6.3.definition: Yeasts ferment sugars into ethanol and CO2.

2.3.6.4.term: Bacteria oxidize ethanol to acetic acid
2.3.6.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Biology › Bacteria oxidize ethanol to acetic acid
2.3.6.4.definition: In kombucha, acetic acid bacteria convert the yeast's ethanol into acetic acid, giving its sourness.

2.3.6.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Science › SCOBY Biology › Gluconic & glucuronic acids
2.3.6.5.definition: Organic acids found in kombucha alongside acetic acid; their levels vary.

2.3.7.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Production › Brewing Process
2.3.7.definition: Brewing Process is a group of 7 entries in the Kombucha Academy, under Production. It includes Sweet tea base (~50–100 g sugar/L), Starter liquid (~10–20%), Initial pH ≤4.6….

2.3.7.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Sweet tea base (~50–100 g sugar/L)
2.3.7.1.definition: Typical sugar range for the kombucha base.

2.3.7.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Starter liquid (~10–20%)
2.3.7.2.definition: Typical share of mature kombucha added to a new batch.

2.3.7.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Initial pH ≤4.6
2.3.7.3.definition: Adding starter liquid to bring the sweet tea to pH 4.6 or lower to protect against pathogens.

2.3.7.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Production › Brewing Process › F1: 7–14 days at ~20–29 °C
2.3.7.4.definition: Typical first-fermentation duration and temperature range.

2.3.7.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Finished pH ~2.5–3.5

2.3.7.6.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Production › Brewing Process › F2: flavor & bottle
2.3.7.6.definition: Second fermentation: flavorings are added and the kombucha is sealed in bottles to carbonate.

2.3.7.7.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Production › Brewing Process › Refrigerate
2.3.7.7.definition: Keeping kombucha cold to slow fermentation and carbonation.

2.3.8.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Alcohol Control
2.3.8.definition: Alcohol Control is a group of 5 entries in the Kombucha Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes Below 0.5% ABV = non-alcoholic (US TTB), Hard kombucha ≥0.5% (TTB-regulated), ABV lab testing….

2.3.8.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Alcohol Control › Below 0.5% ABV = non-alcoholic (US TTB)
2.3.8.1.definition: In the US, drinks with less than 0.5% ABV are not regulated as alcoholic beverages by the TTB.

2.3.8.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Alcohol Control › Hard kombucha ≥0.5% (TTB-regulated)
2.3.8.2.definition: At 0.5% ABV or more, kombucha is an alcoholic beverage under US federal rules.

2.3.8.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Alcohol Control › ABV lab testing
2.3.8.3.definition: Lab measurement of alcohol content, used to confirm kombucha stays under legal non-alcoholic limits.

2.3.8.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Alcohol Control › Cold chain
2.3.8.4.definition: Keeping kombucha refrigerated from production to sale to limit continued fermentation.

2.3.8.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Alcohol Control › Yeast management
2.3.8.5.definition: Controlling the yeast population to manage alcohol and flavor.

2.3.9.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Techniques › Flavoring & Carbonation
2.3.9.definition: Flavoring & Carbonation is a group of 6 entries in the Kombucha Academy, under Techniques. It includes Fruit juice, Whole fruit, Herbs & botanicals….

2.3.9.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Techniques › Flavoring & Carbonation › Fruit juice
2.3.9.1.definition: Juice added in F2 for flavor and extra sugar.

2.3.9.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Techniques › Flavoring & Carbonation › Whole fruit
2.3.9.2.definition: Pieces of fruit added during F2.

2.3.9.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Techniques › Flavoring & Carbonation › Herbs & botanicals

2.3.9.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Techniques › Flavoring & Carbonation › Ginger

2.3.9.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Techniques › Flavoring & Carbonation › Bottle conditioning
2.3.9.5.definition: Carbonating beer (or other drinks) by refermentation in the sealed bottle.

2.3.9.6.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Techniques › Flavoring & Carbonation › Forced carbonation (kegging)
2.3.9.6.definition: Carbonating kombucha by adding CO2 in kegs instead of bottle conditioning.

2.3.10.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Quality & Safety
2.3.10.definition: Quality & Safety is a group of 6 entries in the Kombucha Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes Mold (fuzzy, dry spots), Kahm yeast, Fruit flies….

2.3.10.1.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Quality & Safety › Mold (fuzzy, dry spots)
2.3.10.1.definition: Fuzzy, dry, colored growth on kombucha that means the batch should be discarded.

2.3.10.2.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Quality & Safety › Kahm yeast
2.3.10.2.definition: Harmless but off-flavored film yeast that can form on ferments; flat and wrinkly, unlike fuzzy mold.

2.3.10.3.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Quality & Safety › Fruit flies
2.3.10.3.definition: Insects attracted to fermenting liquid; vessels are covered to keep them out.

2.3.10.4.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Quality & Safety › Vinegar eels
2.3.10.4.definition: Tiny nematodes (Turbatrix aceti) that can live in vinegar and kombucha.

2.3.10.5.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Quality & Safety › Over-acidification
2.3.10.5.definition: Fermenting too long, making kombucha very sour.

2.3.10.6.path: Steep Guild › Kombucha Academy › Quality & Standards › Quality & Safety › Food-safe vessels (no leaded glaze)
2.3.10.6.definition: Kombucha's acidity can leach lead from some ceramic glazes, so glass or food-grade vessels are recommended.

3.1.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Spring Water
3.1.1.definition: Spring Water is a group of 3 entries in the Water Academy. It includes Natural spring, Artesian spring, Glacier/icecap water.

3.1.1.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Spring Water › Natural spring
3.1.1.1.definition: Water from an underground source that flows naturally to the surface.

3.1.1.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Spring Water › Artesian spring
3.1.1.2.definition: Spring fed by a confined aquifer under pressure.

3.1.1.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Spring Water › Glacier/icecap water
3.1.1.3.definition: Bottled water sourced from glaciers or ice caps.

3.1.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Mineral Water
3.1.2.definition: Mineral Water is a group of 4 entries in the Water Academy. It includes Low-mineral (<500 mg/L TDS), Medium-mineral, High-mineral (>1500 mg/L TDS)….

3.1.2.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Mineral Water › Low-mineral (<500 mg/L TDS)
3.1.2.1.definition: In EU labeling, waters at or below 500 mg/L of dissolved solids may be called 'low mineral content'.

3.1.2.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Mineral Water › Medium-mineral
3.1.2.2.definition: Mineral water with moderate dissolved solids, roughly between low-mineral and high-mineral levels.

3.1.2.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Mineral Water › High-mineral (>1500 mg/L TDS)
3.1.2.3.definition: In EU labeling, waters with over 1,500 mg/L of dissolved solids may be called 'rich in mineral salts'.

3.1.2.4.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Mineral Water › Naturally carbonated mineral
3.1.2.4.definition: Mineral water with CO2 from its own source.

3.1.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Sparkling Water
3.1.3.definition: Sparkling Water is a group of 2 entries in the Water Academy. It includes Carbonated (added CO2), Seltzer.

3.1.3.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Sparkling Water › Carbonated (added CO2)

3.1.3.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Sparkling Water › Seltzer

3.1.4.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Purified Water
3.1.4.definition: Purified Water is a group of 3 entries in the Water Academy. It includes Distilled, Reverse osmosis, Deionized.

3.1.4.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Purified Water › Distilled
3.1.4.1.definition: Water boiled and recondensed, leaving minerals behind.

3.1.4.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Purified Water › Reverse osmosis
3.1.4.2.definition: Pushing water through a semi-permeable membrane to remove most dissolved solids.

3.1.4.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Purified Water › Deionized
3.1.4.3.definition: Water with ions removed by ion-exchange resins.

3.1.5.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Functional Water
3.1.5.definition: Functional Water is a group of 4 entries in the Water Academy. It includes Alkaline (ionized), Electrolyte-enhanced, Flavored/infused….

3.1.5.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Functional Water › Alkaline (ionized)
3.1.5.1.definition: Water with a raised pH, made by electrolysis or by adding minerals; its health claims are not well established.

3.1.5.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Functional Water › Electrolyte-enhanced
3.1.5.2.definition: Water with added minerals such as potassium and magnesium, often for taste.

3.1.5.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Functional Water › Flavored/infused
3.1.5.3.definition: Water with added flavors or fruit infusions.

3.1.5.4.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Functional Water › Hydrogen water
3.1.5.4.definition: Water infused with dissolved hydrogen gas; its health benefits are not well established.

3.1.6.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Tap & Treated
3.1.6.definition: Tap & Treated is a group of 5 entries in the Water Academy. It includes Municipal tap water, Private well water, Carbon-filtered….

3.1.6.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Tap & Treated › Municipal tap water
3.1.6.1.definition: Water from public supplies, treated to drinking standards.

3.1.6.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Tap & Treated › Private well water
3.1.6.2.definition: Household wells, which in the US are not regulated by the EPA and are the owner's responsibility to test.

3.1.6.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Tap & Treated › Carbon-filtered

3.1.6.4.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Tap & Treated › Boiled (point-of-use)
3.1.6.4.definition: Boiling water at home to kill pathogens, e.g. under a boil-water advisory.

3.1.6.5.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Tap & Treated › UV-treated

3.1.7.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sources & Hydrogeology
3.1.7.definition: Sources & Hydrogeology is a group of 7 entries in the Water Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Confined aquifers, Unconfined aquifers, Springs….

3.1.7.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sources & Hydrogeology › Confined aquifers
3.1.7.1.definition: Groundwater layers sealed between impermeable rock or clay.

3.1.7.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sources & Hydrogeology › Unconfined aquifers
