3.1.7.2.definition: Groundwater layers open to recharge from the surface above.

3.1.7.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sources & Hydrogeology › Springs

3.1.7.4.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sources & Hydrogeology › Artesian wells
3.1.7.4.definition: Wells tapping a confined aquifer where water rises under its own pressure.

3.1.7.5.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sources & Hydrogeology › Surface water (lakes, rivers)
3.1.7.5.definition: Water sources open to the air, needing more treatment than groundwater.

3.1.7.6.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sources & Hydrogeology › Glacial melt

3.1.7.7.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sources & Hydrogeology › Desalination
3.1.7.7.definition: Removing salt from seawater or brackish water, usually by reverse osmosis or distillation.

3.1.8.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment
3.1.8.definition: Treatment is a group of 10 entries in the Water Academy, under Production. It includes Coagulation & flocculation, Sedimentation, Sand filtration….

3.1.8.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Coagulation & flocculation
3.1.8.1.definition: Treatment steps that clump fine particles so they can settle or be filtered out.

3.1.8.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Sedimentation
3.1.8.2.definition: Letting particles settle out of water.

3.1.8.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Sand filtration
3.1.8.3.definition: Filtering water through sand beds to remove particles.

3.1.8.4.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Activated carbon
3.1.8.4.definition: Porous carbon that adsorbs chlorine, organic compounds and off-tastes from water.

3.1.8.5.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Reverse osmosis
3.1.8.5.definition: Pushing water through a semi-permeable membrane to remove most dissolved solids.

3.1.8.6.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Ion exchange (softening)
3.1.8.6.definition: Swapping calcium and magnesium ions for sodium or potassium to soften water.

3.1.8.7.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › UV disinfection

3.1.8.8.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Ozonation
3.1.8.8.definition: Disinfecting water with ozone, common for bottled water.

3.1.8.9.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Chlorination/chloramination
3.1.8.9.definition: Disinfecting water with chlorine or chloramine, which persists longer.

3.1.8.10.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Production › Treatment › Remineralization
3.1.8.10.definition: Adding minerals back to purified water for taste and stability.

3.1.9.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry
3.1.9.definition: Water Chemistry is a group of 8 entries in the Water Academy, under Science. It includes TDS (mg/L), Hardness (Ca, Mg), Alkalinity (bicarbonate)….

3.1.9.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry › TDS (mg/L)
3.1.9.1.definition: Total dissolved solids, measured in milligrams per liter.

3.1.9.2.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry › Hardness (Ca, Mg)
3.1.9.2.definition: Mainly calcium and magnesium content of water.

3.1.9.3.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry › Alkalinity (bicarbonate)
3.1.9.3.definition: Water's capacity to neutralize acid, mainly from bicarbonate.

3.1.9.4.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry › pH
3.1.9.4.definition: Measure of acidity or alkalinity; drinking water is usually around 6.5–8.5.

3.1.9.5.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry › Sodium
3.1.9.5.definition: Mineral in water that adds salty taste at higher levels.

3.1.9.6.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry › Silica
3.1.9.6.definition: Dissolved silicon dioxide, naturally present in many waters.

3.1.9.7.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry › Nitrate
3.1.9.7.definition: Water contaminant, often from fertilizer; the US EPA limit is 10 mg/L as nitrogen.

3.1.9.8.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Science › Water Chemistry › Conductivity
3.1.9.8.definition: Electrical conductivity of water, a proxy for dissolved minerals.

3.1.10.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Quality & Standards › Standards
3.1.10.definition: Standards is a group of 4 entries in the Water Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes US EPA (Safe Drinking Water Act), US FDA bottled water (21 CFR 165.110), EU Natural Mineral Water Directive….

3.1.10.1.path: Source Guild › Water Academy › Quality & Standards › Standards › US EPA (Safe Drinking Water Act)

3.3.13.2.definition: French-origin dairy goat breed, hardy and high-producing.

3.3.13.3.definition: Dairy goat breed with long, floppy ears and high-butterfat milk.

3.3.14.5.definition: Barns where cows move freely between stalls, feed and water.

3.3.15.definition: Milking is a group of 7 entries in the Milk Academy, under Production. It includes Herringbone parlor, Parallel parlor, Rotary parlor….

3.3.15.1.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Milking › Herringbone parlor
3.3.15.1.definition: Milking parlor where cows stand angled side by side.

3.3.15.2.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Milking › Parallel parlor
3.3.15.2.definition: Milking parlor where cows stand side by side and are milked from behind.

3.3.15.3.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Milking › Rotary parlor
3.3.15.3.definition: Rotating platform for milking many cows.

3.3.15.4.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Milking › Robotic milking (AMS)

3.3.15.5.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Milking › Teat dipping

3.3.15.6.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Milking › Somatic cell count (SCC)
3.3.15.6.definition: Count of white blood cells in milk, an indicator of udder health.

3.3.15.7.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Milking › Bulk tank cooling (≤7 °C / 45 °F)
3.3.15.7.definition: Rapidly chilling raw milk in the farm tank, as required for Grade A milk.

3.3.16.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components
3.3.16.definition: Milk Components is a group of 9 entries in the Milk Academy, under Science. It includes Water (~87%), Fat (~3.5–4%), Protein (~3.3%)….

3.3.16.1.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › Water (~87%)
3.3.16.1.definition: Water makes up about 87% of cow's milk.

3.3.16.2.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › Fat (~3.5–4%)
3.3.16.2.definition: Typical milkfat content of whole cow's milk.

3.3.16.3.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › Protein (~3.3%)
3.3.16.3.definition: Typical protein content of cow's milk.

3.3.16.4.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › Casein (~80% of protein)
3.3.16.4.definition: The main protein group in milk, about 80% of milk protein.

3.3.16.5.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › Whey proteins (~20%)
3.3.16.5.definition: About 20% of milk protein is whey protein.

3.3.16.6.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › Lactose (~4.8%)
3.3.16.6.definition: Typical lactose content of cow's milk.

3.3.16.7.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › Minerals (Ca, P)
3.3.16.7.definition: Milk is a major dietary source of calcium and phosphorus.

3.3.16.8.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › A1 vs A2 β-casein
3.3.16.8.definition: Two common variants of the milk protein β-casein. Some people report digesting A2 milk more comfortably; the evidence is still debated.

3.3.16.9.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Science › Milk Components › Fat globules
3.3.16.9.definition: Microscopic droplets of milkfat surrounded by membranes.

3.3.17.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps
3.3.17.definition: Processing Steps is a group of 10 entries in the Milk Academy, under Production. It includes Receiving & testing, Clarification, Separation (cream/skim)….

3.3.17.1.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Receiving & testing
3.3.17.1.definition: Checking incoming milk for temperature, residues and quality.

3.3.17.2.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Clarification
3.3.17.2.definition: Centrifuging milk to remove sediment and some cells.

3.3.17.3.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Separation (cream/skim)
3.3.17.3.definition: Centrifugally separating cream from skim milk.

3.3.17.4.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Standardization
3.3.17.4.definition: Adjusting milkfat to a target level.

3.3.17.5.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Homogenization
3.3.17.5.definition: Forcing milk through small openings under pressure to shrink fat globules so cream does not separate.

3.3.17.6.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › HTST (72 °C / 15 s)
3.3.17.6.definition: High-temperature short-time pasteurization: at least 72 °C for 15 seconds.

3.3.17.7.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Ultra-pasteurization (≥138 °C / 2 s)
3.3.17.7.definition: US ultra-pasteurization: heating to at least 138 °C for at least 2 seconds.

3.3.17.8.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › UHT aseptic
3.3.17.8.definition: Milk treated at ultra-high temperature and packed sterile so it is shelf-stable.

3.3.17.9.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › ESL (extended shelf life)
3.3.17.9.definition: Refrigerated milk processed with higher heat or microfiltration to last weeks longer than standard pasteurized milk.

3.3.17.10.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Processing Steps › Microfiltration
3.3.17.10.definition: Membrane filtration that removes bacteria and extends shelf life.

3.3.18.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Quality & Standards › Grading & Regulation
3.3.18.definition: Grading & Regulation is a group of 5 entries in the Milk Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes Grade A (Pasteurized Milk Ordinance), Manufacturing grade (Grade B), Antibiotic residue testing….

3.3.18.1.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Quality & Standards › Grading & Regulation › Grade A (Pasteurized Milk Ordinance)
3.3.18.1.definition: US standard for fluid milk under the FDA's Pasteurized Milk Ordinance (PMO).

3.3.18.2.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Quality & Standards › Grading & Regulation › Manufacturing grade (Grade B)
3.3.18.2.definition: Milk for cheese, butter and powders rather than fluid sale.

3.3.18.3.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Quality & Standards › Grading & Regulation › Antibiotic residue testing
3.3.18.3.definition: Required testing of milk, e.g. tanker loads, for drug residues before it is accepted.

3.3.18.4.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Quality & Standards › Grading & Regulation › Bacteria count limits
3.3.18.4.definition: Maximum bacterial counts for raw and pasteurized milk set by standards such as the US Pasteurized Milk Ordinance.

3.3.18.5.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Quality & Standards › Grading & Regulation › Raw milk sales (state law)
3.3.18.5.definition: In the US, raw-milk retail sales are set by each state; interstate sale for direct consumption is banned federally.

3.3.19.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Plant Milk Production
3.3.19.definition: Plant Milk Production is a group of 7 entries in the Milk Academy, under Production. It includes Soaking, Wet milling, Enzymatic hydrolysis (oat)….

3.3.19.1.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Plant Milk Production › Soaking
3.3.19.1.definition: Hydrating nuts, seeds or grains before milling them into plant milk.

3.3.19.2.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Plant Milk Production › Wet milling
3.3.19.2.definition: Grinding soaked ingredients with water for plant milk.

3.3.19.3.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Plant Milk Production › Enzymatic hydrolysis (oat)
3.3.19.3.definition: Using enzymes to break oat starch into sugars, making oat milk naturally sweet and smooth.

3.3.19.4.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Plant Milk Production › Filtering/decanting
3.3.19.4.definition: Separating plant-milk liquid from the solid pulp.

3.3.19.5.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Plant Milk Production › Fortification (Ca, D, B12)
3.3.19.5.definition: Adding nutrients such as calcium, vitamin D and vitamin B12, common in plant milks.

3.3.19.6.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Plant Milk Production › Homogenization
3.3.19.6.definition: Forcing milk through small openings under pressure to shrink fat globules so cream does not separate.

3.3.19.7.path: Source Guild › Milk Academy › Production › Plant Milk Production › UHT
3.3.19.7.definition: Ultra-high-temperature treatment, about 135–150 °C for a few seconds, packaged aseptically for shelf stability.

4.1.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Hydration & Electrolytes
4.1.1.definition: Hydration & Electrolytes is a group of 4 entries in the Health Academy. It includes Oral rehydration solution (WHO ORS), Isotonic sports drinks, Hypotonic electrolyte drinks….

4.1.1.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Hydration & Electrolytes › Oral rehydration solution (WHO ORS)
4.1.1.1.definition: WHO formula of glucose and salts that uses sodium-glucose co-transport to rehydrate.

4.1.1.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Hydration & Electrolytes › Isotonic sports drinks
4.1.1.2.definition: Drinks with concentration similar to body fluids (about 6–8% carbohydrate), supplying fluid, sugar and electrolytes.

4.1.1.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Hydration & Electrolytes › Hypotonic electrolyte drinks
4.1.1.3.definition: Drinks less concentrated than body fluids, designed for fast fluid absorption.

4.1.1.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Hydration & Electrolytes › Electrolyte powders/tablets
4.1.1.4.definition: Mixes of sodium, potassium and other salts dissolved in water for hydration.

4.1.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Gut Health
4.1.2.definition: Gut Health is a group of 3 entries in the Health Academy. It includes Probiotic shots, Prebiotic/fiber drinks, Apple cider vinegar drinks.

4.1.2.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Gut Health › Probiotic shots
4.1.2.1.definition: Small drinks containing live microorganisms; effects are strain-specific.

4.1.2.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Gut Health › Prebiotic/fiber drinks

4.1.2.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Gut Health › Apple cider vinegar drinks
4.1.2.3.definition: Diluted apple cider vinegar drinks. Evidence for health effects is limited, and undiluted vinegar can harm tooth enamel.

4.1.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Functional Wellness
4.1.3.definition: Functional Wellness is a group of 5 entries in the Health Academy. It includes Vitamin-enhanced water, Collagen drinks, Ginger/turmeric shots….

4.1.3.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Functional Wellness › Vitamin-enhanced water
4.1.3.1.definition: Water with added vitamins and often sugar or sweeteners.

4.1.3.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Functional Wellness › Collagen drinks
4.1.3.2.definition: Drinks containing hydrolyzed collagen peptides, mostly marketed for skin and joints; the evidence is still emerging.

4.1.3.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Functional Wellness › Ginger/turmeric shots
4.1.3.3.definition: Small concentrated juice shots of ginger and turmeric.

4.1.3.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Functional Wellness › Golden milk (turmeric latte)
4.1.3.4.definition: Milk drink spiced with turmeric and other spices.

4.1.3.5.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Functional Wellness › Mushroom elixirs (reishi/chaga)
4.1.3.5.definition: Drinks made with medicinal-mushroom extracts; human evidence is limited.

4.1.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Relaxation & Sleep
4.1.4.definition: Relaxation & Sleep is a group of 4 entries in the Health Academy. It includes Magnesium drinks, L-theanine drinks, Melatonin drinks….

4.1.4.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Relaxation & Sleep › Magnesium drinks
4.1.4.1.definition: Drinks with added magnesium, often marketed for relaxation.

4.1.4.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Relaxation & Sleep › L-theanine drinks
4.1.4.2.definition: Drinks containing L-theanine, an amino acid found in tea.

4.1.4.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Relaxation & Sleep › Melatonin drinks
4.1.4.3.definition: Drinks containing the sleep hormone melatonin; their legal status differs by country.

4.1.4.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Relaxation & Sleep › Adaptogenic drinks (ashwagandha)
4.1.4.4.definition: Drinks containing herbs marketed as 'adaptogens'. The term is not a recognized scientific or regulatory category, and the evidence varies by ingredient.

4.1.5.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Medical Nutrition
4.1.5.definition: Medical Nutrition is a group of 4 entries in the Health Academy. It includes Oral nutritional supplements, Diabetes-specific formulas, Infant formula….

4.1.5.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Medical Nutrition › Oral nutritional supplements
4.1.5.1.definition: Nutrient-dense drinks for people at risk of malnutrition.

4.1.5.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Medical Nutrition › Diabetes-specific formulas
4.1.5.2.definition: Nutritional drinks formulated for blood-glucose management.

4.1.5.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Medical Nutrition › Infant formula
4.1.5.3.definition: Breast-milk substitute regulated under strict nutrient requirements (e.g. 21 CFR 107 in the US).

4.1.5.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Medical Nutrition › Thickened liquids (IDDSI levels 1–4)
4.1.5.4.definition: Drinks thickened to IDDSI levels (slightly to extremely thick) for people with swallowing difficulties.

4.1.6.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Electrolyte Science
4.1.6.definition: Electrolyte Science is a group of 7 entries in the Health Academy, under Science. It includes Sodium, Potassium, Chloride….

4.1.6.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Electrolyte Science › Sodium
4.1.6.1.definition: Main electrolyte lost in sweat and key to rehydration.

4.1.6.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Electrolyte Science › Potassium
4.1.6.2.definition: Electrolyte lost in sweat, included in rehydration drinks.

4.1.6.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Electrolyte Science › Chloride
4.1.6.3.definition: Electrolyte that pairs with sodium in rehydration drinks.

4.1.6.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Electrolyte Science › Magnesium
4.1.6.4.definition: Mineral involved in muscle and nerve function.

4.1.6.5.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Electrolyte Science › Calcium
4.1.6.5.definition: Mineral essential for bones and muscle function, sometimes added to drinks.

4.1.6.6.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Electrolyte Science › Osmolality (hypo/iso/hypertonic)
4.1.6.6.definition: Concentration of dissolved particles compared with body fluids.

4.1.6.7.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Electrolyte Science › Glucose-sodium co-transport (SGLT1)
4.1.6.7.definition: Intestinal transporter that absorbs sodium together with glucose, pulling water along. This is the basis of oral rehydration therapy.

4.1.7.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Functional Ingredients
4.1.7.definition: Functional Ingredients is a group of 7 entries in the Health Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Probiotic strains (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium), Prebiotic fibers (inulin, FOS), Collagen peptides….

4.1.7.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Functional Ingredients › Probiotic strains (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium)
4.1.7.1.definition: Common probiotic genera; benefits depend on the specific strain and dose.

4.1.7.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Functional Ingredients › Prebiotic fibers (inulin, FOS)
4.1.7.2.definition: Fermentable fibers that feed beneficial gut bacteria.

4.1.7.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Functional Ingredients › Collagen peptides
4.1.7.3.definition: Hydrolyzed collagen protein. It is low in some essential amino acids, so it is an incomplete protein.

4.1.7.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Functional Ingredients › Ashwagandha
4.1.7.4.definition: Herb (Withania somnifera) from Ayurvedic tradition, studied for stress and sleep with mixed-quality evidence.

4.1.7.5.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Functional Ingredients › Curcumin (turmeric)
4.1.7.5.definition: Main colored compound in turmeric. It is poorly absorbed on its own, and its health effects are still under study.

4.1.7.6.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Functional Ingredients › Ginger
4.1.7.6.definition: Rhizome used in drinks; it has some evidence for easing nausea.

4.1.7.7.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Functional Ingredients › Acetic acid (vinegar)
4.1.7.7.definition: The main acid in vinegar and the active component in vinegar drinks.

4.1.8.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation
4.1.8.definition: Regulation is a group of 5 entries in the Health Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes Conventional food vs dietary supplement (DSHEA), Structure/function claims, FDA health claims….

4.1.8.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation › Conventional food vs dietary supplement (DSHEA)
4.1.8.1.definition: The US Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act (1994) separates supplements from conventional foods, with different labeling and ingredient rules.

4.1.8.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation › Structure/function claims
4.1.8.2.definition: US claims about effects on the body's structure or function (not disease); supplements must carry a disclaimer.

4.1.8.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation › FDA health claims
4.1.8.3.definition: FDA-authorized claims linking a food substance to reduced disease risk, which require significant scientific agreement or qualified wording.

4.1.8.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation › Supplement Facts vs Nutrition Facts
4.1.8.4.definition: US supplements use a Supplement Facts panel, while foods and beverages use Nutrition Facts.

4.1.8.5.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation › Medical foods
4.1.8.5.definition: US category of foods for the dietary management of a disease, used under medical supervision.

4.1.9.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Evidence Levels
4.1.9.definition: Evidence Levels is a group of 5 entries in the Health Academy, under Science. It includes Meta-analyses & systematic reviews, Randomized controlled trials, Observational studies….

4.1.9.1.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Evidence Levels › Meta-analyses & systematic reviews
4.1.9.1.definition: Studies that pool and evaluate many trials; usually the highest tier of evidence.

4.1.9.2.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Evidence Levels › Randomized controlled trials
4.1.9.2.definition: Experiments with random assignment to groups, giving strong evidence of cause and effect.

4.1.9.3.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Evidence Levels › Observational studies
4.1.9.3.definition: Studies that track people without intervening; they show associations, not causation.

4.1.9.4.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Evidence Levels › Mechanistic & animal studies
4.1.9.4.definition: Lab and animal research that suggests how something might work but doesn't prove effects in humans.

4.1.9.5.path: Energy Guild › Health Academy › Science › Evidence Levels › Expert opinion
4.1.9.5.definition: The lowest tier of the evidence hierarchy.

4.2.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Dairy Proteins
4.2.1.definition: Dairy Proteins is a group of 5 entries in the Protein Academy. It includes Whey protein concentrate, Whey protein isolate, Hydrolyzed whey….

4.2.1.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Dairy Proteins › Whey protein concentrate

4.2.1.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Dairy Proteins › Whey protein isolate
4.2.1.2.definition: Whey processed to at least 90% protein, with most lactose and fat removed.

4.2.1.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Dairy Proteins › Hydrolyzed whey
4.2.1.3.definition: Whey pre-digested into peptides for faster absorption; it tastes more bitter.

4.2.1.4.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Dairy Proteins › Micellar casein
4.2.1.4.definition: Slow-digesting casein protein in its natural micelle form.

4.2.1.5.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Dairy Proteins › Milk protein isolate
4.2.1.5.definition: Milk protein containing both casein and whey.

4.2.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Plant Proteins
4.2.2.definition: Plant Proteins is a group of 6 entries in the Protein Academy. It includes Pea, Soy isolate, Brown rice….

4.2.2.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Plant Proteins › Pea
4.2.2.1.definition: Protein made from yellow pea, the most common plant protein base.

4.2.2.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Plant Proteins › Soy isolate
4.2.2.2.definition: Soy protein concentrated to about 90% protein; a complete protein.

4.2.2.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Plant Proteins › Brown rice
4.2.2.3.definition: Plant protein made from brown rice, often blended with pea.

4.2.2.4.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Plant Proteins › Hemp
4.2.2.4.definition: Protein powder made from hemp seed.

4.2.2.5.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Plant Proteins › Pumpkin seed

4.2.2.6.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Plant Proteins › Blended plant protein
4.2.2.6.definition: Mixes of plant proteins, such as pea and rice, that complement each other's amino acids.

4.2.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Other Proteins
4.2.3.definition: Other Proteins is a group of 3 entries in the Protein Academy. It includes Egg white protein, Collagen peptides, Beef protein isolate.

4.2.3.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Other Proteins › Egg white protein
4.2.3.1.definition: Protein powder made from dried egg whites.

4.2.3.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Other Proteins › Collagen peptides
4.2.3.2.definition: Hydrolyzed collagen protein. It lacks tryptophan, so it does not count as a complete protein.

4.2.3.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Other Proteins › Beef protein isolate
4.2.3.3.definition: Protein powder made from hydrolyzed beef protein.

4.2.4.definition: Formats is a group of 6 entries in the Protein Academy. It includes Powder (mix-in), Ready-to-drink (RTD) shake, Clear whey isolate drinks….

4.2.4.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Formats › Powder (mix-in)
4.2.4.1.definition: Protein sold as powder to mix into liquids.

4.2.4.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Formats › Ready-to-drink (RTD) shake

4.2.4.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Formats › Clear whey isolate drinks
4.2.4.3.definition: Acidified, juice-like drinks made with whey isolate.

4.2.4.4.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Formats › Protein coffee

4.2.4.5.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Formats › High-protein ultra-filtered milk
4.2.4.5.definition: Milk concentrated by ultrafiltration so it has more protein and less lactose.

4.2.4.6.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Formats › Meal replacement shake
4.2.4.6.definition: Nutritionally complete shake designed to replace a meal.

4.2.5.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Use Cases
4.2.5.definition: Use Cases is a group of 4 entries in the Protein Academy. It includes Post-workout recovery, Mass gainer, Weight management….

4.2.5.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Use Cases › Post-workout recovery
4.2.5.1.definition: Protein and carbohydrate taken after exercise to support recovery.

4.2.5.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Use Cases › Mass gainer

4.2.5.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Use Cases › Weight management
4.2.5.3.definition: Products marketed for satiety or calorie control.

4.2.5.4.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Use Cases › Overnight (casein)
4.2.5.4.definition: Casein taken before sleep for slow amino acid release.

4.2.6.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing
4.2.6.definition: Protein Processing is a group of 8 entries in the Protein Academy, under Production. It includes Microfiltration, Ultrafiltration, Ion exchange….

4.2.6.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing › Microfiltration
4.2.6.1.definition: Membrane filtration that produces whey isolate.

4.2.6.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing › Ultrafiltration

4.2.6.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing › Ion exchange
4.2.6.3.definition: Whey isolate process that separates proteins by charge.

4.2.6.4.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing › Enzymatic hydrolysis
4.2.6.4.definition: Using enzymes to break proteins into smaller peptides.

4.2.6.5.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing › Spray drying
4.2.6.5.definition: Drying liquid protein into powder with hot air.

4.2.6.6.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing › Instantizing (lecithin)
4.2.6.6.definition: Coating powders with lecithin so they mix easily.

4.2.6.7.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing › Concentrate (WPC 34–80%)
4.2.6.7.definition: Whey protein concentrate containing about 34–80% protein.

4.2.6.8.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Production › Protein Processing › Isolate (≥90% protein)
4.2.6.8.definition: Protein ingredient containing at least about 90% protein.

4.2.7.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Science › Protein Quality Science
4.2.7.definition: Protein Quality Science is a group of 6 entries in the Protein Academy, under Science. It includes PDCAAS, DIAAS, Leucine content….

4.2.7.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Science › Protein Quality Science › PDCAAS
4.2.7.1.definition: Protein Digestibility-Corrected Amino Acid Score, a protein-quality measure capped at 1.0.

4.2.7.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Science › Protein Quality Science › DIAAS
4.2.7.2.definition: Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score, a newer FAO-recommended protein-quality measure.

4.2.7.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Science › Protein Quality Science › Leucine content
4.2.7.3.definition: Leucine is an amino acid that triggers muscle protein synthesis; whey is rich in it.

4.2.7.4.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Science › Protein Quality Science › Essential amino acids
4.2.7.4.definition: The nine amino acids the body cannot make and must get from food.

4.2.7.5.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Science › Protein Quality Science › Fast (whey) vs slow (casein) digestion
4.2.7.5.definition: Whey is absorbed quickly, while casein clots in the stomach and digests slowly.

4.2.7.6.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Science › Protein Quality Science › Branched-chain amino acids
4.2.7.6.definition: Leucine, isoleucine and valine; essential amino acids marketed for muscle.

4.2.8.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Techniques › Formulation
4.2.8.definition: Formulation is a group of 5 entries in the Protein Academy, under Techniques. It includes Heat stability (UHT RTD), Emulsifiers & stabilizers, Sweeteners….

4.2.8.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Techniques › Formulation › Heat stability (UHT RTD)
4.2.8.1.definition: A protein's ability to survive UHT processing without gelling or settling.

4.2.8.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Techniques › Formulation › Emulsifiers & stabilizers
4.2.8.2.definition: Ingredients such as lecithin and gums that keep protein drinks smooth and stable.

4.2.8.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Techniques › Formulation › Sweeteners
4.2.8.3.definition: Sugars or non-nutritive sweeteners used in protein drinks.

4.2.8.4.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Techniques › Formulation › Flavor masking
4.2.8.4.definition: Hiding off-flavors of proteins with flavors and sweeteners.

4.2.8.5.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Techniques › Formulation › Protein per serving
4.2.8.5.definition: Grams of protein in one serving.

4.2.9.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation & Testing
4.2.9.definition: Regulation & Testing is a group of 4 entries in the Protein Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes FDA protein claims (good/excellent source), Supplement vs conventional food, NSF Certified for Sport….

4.2.9.1.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation & Testing › FDA protein claims (good/excellent source)
4.2.9.1.definition: US labels: 'good source' means 10–19% of the Daily Value per serving, 'excellent source' means 20% or more.

4.2.9.2.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation & Testing › Supplement vs conventional food
4.2.9.2.definition: US regulatory distinction between supplements and ordinary foods or drinks, affecting labels and allowed ingredients.

4.2.9.3.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation & Testing › NSF Certified for Sport
4.2.9.3.definition: NSF program that tests supplements for contaminants and banned substances.

4.2.9.4.path: Energy Guild › Protein Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation & Testing › Informed Sport
4.2.9.4.definition: Third-party testing program that screens supplements for banned substances.

4.3.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Energy Drinks
4.3.1.definition: Energy Drinks is a group of 5 entries in the Energy Academy. It includes Standard energy drink, Sugar-free/zero, Energy shots….

4.3.1.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Energy Drinks › Standard energy drink
4.3.1.1.definition: Caffeinated carbonated drink, often with taurine and B vitamins.

4.3.1.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Energy Drinks › Sugar-free/zero
4.3.1.2.definition: Energy drinks sweetened with non-nutritive sweeteners.

4.3.1.3.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Energy Drinks › Energy shots

4.3.1.4.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Energy Drinks › Fitness/performance energy

4.3.1.5.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Energy Drinks › Natural/organic energy
4.3.1.5.definition: Energy drinks using natural caffeine sources such as tea or guayusa.

4.3.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Caffeine Sources
4.3.2.definition: Caffeine Sources is a group of 6 entries in the Energy Academy. It includes Caffeine anhydrous, Guarana, Green coffee extract….

4.3.2.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Caffeine Sources › Caffeine anhydrous
4.3.2.1.definition: Dehydrated, purified caffeine powder used in drinks and supplements.

4.3.2.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Caffeine Sources › Guarana
4.3.2.2.definition: Amazonian plant whose seeds are a natural caffeine source.

4.3.2.3.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Caffeine Sources › Green coffee extract

4.3.2.4.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Caffeine Sources › Green tea extract
4.3.2.4.definition: Caffeine and catechin source from green tea.

4.3.2.5.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Caffeine Sources › Guayusa
4.3.2.5.definition: Caffeinated holly leaf (Ilex guayusa) from Ecuador.

4.3.2.6.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Caffeine Sources › Kola nut

4.3.3.definition: Pre-Workout is a group of 5 entries in the Energy Academy. It includes Stimulant pre-workout, Stim-free (pump) pre-workout, Beta-alanine….

4.3.3.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Pre-Workout › Stimulant pre-workout
4.3.3.1.definition: Pre-workout with caffeine and other stimulants.

4.3.3.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Pre-Workout › Stim-free (pump) pre-workout
4.3.3.2.definition: Pre-workout without stimulants, focused on blood flow.

4.3.3.3.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Pre-Workout › Beta-alanine
4.3.3.3.definition: Amino acid that raises muscle carnosine; it causes a harmless tingling (paresthesia).

4.3.3.4.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Pre-Workout › Creatine monohydrate
4.3.3.4.definition: Well-researched supplement that improves high-intensity exercise performance.

4.3.3.5.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Pre-Workout › L-citrulline
4.3.3.5.definition: Amino acid in pre-workouts, studied for blood flow.

4.3.4.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › RTD Caffeinated
4.3.4.definition: RTD Caffeinated is a group of 4 entries in the Energy Academy. It includes Canned cold brew, Nitro coffee, RTD tea….

4.3.4.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › RTD Caffeinated › Canned cold brew
4.3.4.1.definition: Ready-to-drink cold brew coffee in cans.

4.3.4.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › RTD Caffeinated › Nitro coffee

4.3.4.3.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › RTD Caffeinated › RTD tea

4.3.4.4.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › RTD Caffeinated › Caffeinated sparkling water

4.3.5.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Focus & Nootropic
4.3.5.definition: Focus & Nootropic is a group of 3 entries in the Energy Academy. It includes Caffeine + L-theanine, Citicoline/Alpha-GPC drinks, Lion's mane drinks.

4.3.5.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Focus & Nootropic › Caffeine + L-theanine
4.3.5.1.definition: Combination studied for focus; theanine may soften caffeine's jitteriness.

4.3.5.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Focus & Nootropic › Citicoline/Alpha-GPC drinks
4.3.5.2.definition: Drinks with choline compounds marketed for cognition; the evidence is limited.

4.3.5.3.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Focus & Nootropic › Lion's mane drinks
4.3.5.3.definition: Drinks with Hericium erinaceus mushroom extract; human evidence is limited.

4.3.6.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Science › Caffeine Science
4.3.6.definition: Caffeine Science is a group of 6 entries in the Energy Academy, under Science. It includes Adenosine receptor antagonism, Half-life (~3–7 h), ~80 mg per 250 mL can….

4.3.6.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Science › Caffeine Science › Adenosine receptor antagonism
4.3.6.1.definition: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors in the brain, reducing feelings of tiredness.

4.3.6.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Science › Caffeine Science › Half-life (~3–7 h)
4.3.6.2.definition: Typical caffeine half-life in healthy adults; it varies widely.

4.3.6.3.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Science › Caffeine Science › ~80 mg per 250 mL can
4.3.6.3.definition: Typical caffeine in a standard 250 mL energy drink.

4.3.6.4.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Science › Caffeine Science › FDA: ~400 mg/day healthy adults
4.3.6.4.definition: The FDA cites 400 mg of caffeine a day as an amount not generally associated with negative effects in healthy adults.

4.3.6.5.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Science › Caffeine Science › EFSA: 200 mg single dose
4.3.6.5.definition: EFSA concluded that single caffeine doses up to 200 mg are of no safety concern for healthy adults.

4.3.6.6.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Science › Caffeine Science › CYP1A2 metabolism
4.3.6.6.definition: Liver enzyme that metabolizes most caffeine; genetic variation affects how fast caffeine is cleared.

4.3.7.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Other Ingredients
4.3.7.definition: Other Ingredients is a group of 7 entries in the Energy Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Taurine, B vitamins, Glucuronolactone….

4.3.7.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Other Ingredients › Taurine
4.3.7.1.definition: Amino sulfonic acid commonly added to energy drinks.

4.3.7.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Other Ingredients › B vitamins
4.3.7.2.definition: Vitamins involved in energy metabolism; they are not stimulants.

4.3.7.3.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Other Ingredients › Glucuronolactone
4.3.7.3.definition: Naturally occurring compound added to energy drinks.

4.3.7.4.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Other Ingredients › Ginseng
4.3.7.4.definition: Panax root extract, common in energy drinks.

4.3.7.5.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Other Ingredients › L-carnitine
4.3.7.5.definition: Compound involved in fat transport into cells, often added to energy drinks.

4.3.7.6.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Other Ingredients › Sugar vs non-nutritive sweeteners
4.3.7.6.definition: Choice between caloric sugar and zero-calorie sweeteners.

4.3.7.7.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Other Ingredients › Electrolytes
4.3.7.7.definition: Minerals added to some energy and fitness drinks.

4.3.8.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation
4.3.8.definition: Regulation is a group of 4 entries in the Energy Academy, under Quality & Standards. It includes Beverage vs supplement labeling, Caffeine disclosure, EU 'high caffeine content' label (>150 mg/L)….

4.3.8.1.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation › Beverage vs supplement labeling

4.3.8.2.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation › Caffeine disclosure
4.3.8.2.definition: Stating caffeine content on labels, required in some markets and voluntary in others.

4.3.8.3.definition: EU rule requiring a high-caffeine warning on drinks with more than 150 mg/L of caffeine, with tea and coffee exempt.

4.3.8.4.term: Restrictions on sales to minors (some countries)
4.3.8.4.path: Energy Guild › Energy Academy › Quality & Standards › Regulation › Restrictions on sales to minors (some countries)

5.1.1.3.definition: North American soda traditionally flavored with sassafras root bark; commercial versions use safrole-free flavoring.

5.1.1.4.definition: Ginger-flavored carbonated soft drink; dry (Canadian) and golden styles.

5.1.1.9.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Classic Soda Styles › Birch beer
5.1.1.9.definition: Soda flavored with birch bark or oil, related to root beer.

5.1.1.10.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Classic Soda Styles › Sarsaparilla
5.1.1.10.definition: Soda traditionally flavored with sarsaparilla root.

5.1.4.1.definition: Concentrated fruit drink diluted with water.

5.1.4.2.definition: Concentrated sweetened fruit syrup; in some countries the word also means a liqueur.

5.1.4.4.definition: Concentrated flavored syrup for making soda.

5.1.5.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Carbonation Methods
5.1.5.definition: Carbonation Methods is a group of 5 entries in the Carbonated Academy. It includes Forced carbonation (CO2), Natural carbonation (bottle-conditioned), Nitrogenation (nitro)….

5.1.5.1.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Carbonation Methods › Forced carbonation (CO2)
5.1.5.1.definition: Dissolving CO2 into liquid under pressure.

5.1.5.2.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Carbonation Methods › Natural carbonation (bottle-conditioned)
5.1.5.2.definition: CO2 produced by fermentation inside the sealed bottle.

5.1.5.3.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Carbonation Methods › Nitrogenation (nitro)
5.1.5.3.definition: Infusing drinks with nitrogen for small bubbles and a creamy texture.

5.1.5.4.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Carbonation Methods › Post-mix (fountain)
5.1.5.4.definition: Syrup and carbonated water mixed when served.

5.1.5.5.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Carbonation Methods › Pre-mix (bottle/can)
5.1.5.5.definition: Soda fully mixed and carbonated before packaging.

5.1.6.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Science › Carbonation Science
5.1.6.definition: Carbonation Science is a group of 6 entries in the Carbonated Academy, under Science. It includes CO2 solubility (Henry's law), Volumes of CO2, Soda ~2.5–4 volumes….

5.1.6.1.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Science › Carbonation Science › CO2 solubility (Henry's law)
5.1.6.1.definition: More CO2 dissolves in colder liquid and under higher pressure.

5.1.6.2.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Science › Carbonation Science › Volumes of CO2
5.1.6.2.definition: Measure of carbonation: liters of CO2 dissolved per liter of liquid.

5.1.6.3.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Science › Carbonation Science › Soda ~2.5–4 volumes
5.1.6.3.definition: Typical carbonation level of soft drinks.

5.1.6.4.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Science › Carbonation Science › Temperature & pressure

5.1.6.5.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Science › Carbonation Science › Carbonic acid
5.1.6.5.definition: Weak acid formed when CO2 dissolves in water, adding bite.

5.1.6.6.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Science › Carbonation Science › Nucleation & bubble retention
5.1.6.6.definition: Bubbles form at nucleation sites; temperature and surface affect how long fizz lasts.

5.1.7.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Syrup Making
5.1.7.definition: Syrup Making is a group of 6 entries in the Carbonated Academy, under Production. It includes Simple syrup, Flavor concentrates & emulsions, Throw ratio (e.g. 1:5)….

5.1.7.1.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Syrup Making › Simple syrup

5.1.7.2.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Syrup Making › Flavor concentrates & emulsions
5.1.7.2.definition: Concentrated flavorings; emulsions disperse oil-based flavors such as citrus oils in water.

5.1.7.3.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Syrup Making › Throw ratio (e.g. 1:5)
5.1.7.3.definition: Ratio of syrup to water in finished soda.

5.1.7.4.definition: Target sugar levels in syrup or finished soda.

5.1.7.5.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Syrup Making › Batch mixing
5.1.7.5.definition: Combining syrup ingredients in batches before filling.

5.1.7.6.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Syrup Making › Bag-in-box (post-mix)
5.1.7.6.definition: Syrup packed in bags inside boxes for fountain systems.

5.1.8.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners
5.1.8.definition: Sweeteners is a group of 9 entries in the Carbonated Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Sucrose (cane sugar), HFCS 55, Aspartame….

5.1.8.1.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › Sucrose (cane sugar)
5.1.8.1.definition: Table sugar from sugarcane or sugar beet.

5.1.8.2.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › HFCS 55
5.1.8.2.definition: High-fructose corn syrup with about 55% fructose, the common US soda sweetener.

5.1.8.3.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › Aspartame
5.1.8.3.definition: Low-calorie sweetener about 200 times sweeter than sugar. People with phenylketonuria (PKU) must avoid it.

5.1.8.4.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › Sucralose
5.1.8.4.definition: Zero-calorie sweetener about 600 times sweeter than sugar.

5.1.8.5.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › Acesulfame K
5.1.8.5.definition: Zero-calorie sweetener about 200 times sweeter than sugar, often paired with others.

5.1.8.6.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › Stevia (Reb M)
5.1.8.6.definition: Sweetener from the stevia leaf; Reb M is a better-tasting steviol glycoside.

5.1.8.7.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › Monk fruit
5.1.8.7.definition: Zero-calorie sweetener from luo han guo fruit extract (mogrosides).

5.1.8.8.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › Erythritol
5.1.8.8.definition: Sugar alcohol with nearly zero calories.

5.1.8.9.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Sweeteners › Allulose
5.1.8.9.definition: Rare sugar with very few calories; it is about 70% as sweet as sugar.

5.1.9.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Acids & Preservatives
5.1.9.definition: Acids & Preservatives is a group of 6 entries in the Carbonated Academy, under Cultivation & Raw Materials. It includes Phosphoric acid (colas), Citric acid, Malic acid….

5.1.9.1.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Acids & Preservatives › Phosphoric acid (colas)
5.1.9.1.definition: Acid that gives colas their sharp tang.

5.1.9.2.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Acids & Preservatives › Citric acid
5.1.9.2.definition: Common soda acidulant that gives citrus-like sourness.

5.1.9.3.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Acids & Preservatives › Malic acid
5.1.9.3.definition: Acid found naturally in apples, used in sodas.

5.1.9.4.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Acids & Preservatives › Tartaric acid
5.1.9.4.definition: Grape-derived acid sometimes used in drinks.

5.1.9.5.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Acids & Preservatives › Sodium benzoate

5.1.9.6.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Cultivation & Raw Materials › Acids & Preservatives › Potassium sorbate
5.1.9.6.definition: Preservative that inhibits mold and yeast.

5.1.10.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Packaging

5.1.10.1.definition: Inert, reusable or recyclable soda container.

5.1.10.2.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Packaging › Aluminum can
5.1.10.2.definition: Lightweight, recyclable can that blocks light and oxygen.

5.1.10.4.path: Culture Guild › Carbonated Academy › Production › Packaging › Fountain (post-mix)
5.1.10.4.definition: Soda mixed from syrup and carbonated water at the point of service.

5.2.1.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Sake Grades (Tokutei Meishoshu)

5.2.1.1.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Sake Grades (Tokutei Meishoshu) › Junmai Daiginjo
5.2.1.1.definition: Pure-rice sake with rice polished to 50% or less.

5.2.1.2.definition: Premium sake grade with rice polished to 50% or less.

5.2.1.3.definition: Pure-rice sake with rice polished to 60% or less.

5.2.1.4.definition: Premium sake grade with rice polished to 60% or less of its original size.

5.2.1.8.definition: Sake with a small permitted addition of distilled alcohol and rice polished to 70% or less.

5.2.2.7.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Sake Styles › Sparkling sake

5.2.5.8.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Mead › Hydromel (session)

5.2.6.1.definition: Sake aged in Japanese cedar casks.

5.2.6.3.definition: Traditional cider fermented or matured in old oak vats.

5.2.6.4.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Barrel Toasting & Aging › Barrel & Wood Aging › Barrel-aged mead

5.2.7.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Fermented Milks
5.2.7.definition: Fermented Milks is a group of 4 entries in the Fermented Academy. It includes Milk kefir, Kumis (mare's milk), Drinkable yogurt….

5.2.9.1.definition: Fermented sugar-water drink made with water kefir grains.

5.2.9.3.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Plant & Fruit Ferments › Pulque

5.2.9.4.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Plant & Fruit Ferments › Ginger beer (ginger bug)

5.2.9.5.path: Culture Guild › Fermented Academy › Plant & Fruit Ferments › Palm wine
